section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How often must motor vehicles registered in New Hampshire be inspected?
options: a:Once a year, during the registered owner's birth month.,b:Once every two years.,c:Annually by July 1st.
note: In New Hampshire, registered vehicles must be inspected once a year, and the inspection must be completed during the registered owner's birth month.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Who is required by law to wear a seat belt in a moving vehicle in New Hampshire?
options: a:Anyone under the age of 18.,b:All occupants, including the driver, regardless of age.,c:Only the driver and front seat passengers.
note: In New Hampshire, anyone under the age of 18 is required by law to wear a seat belt. New Hampshire is the only U.S. state that does not legally require adults (18 and older) to wear seat belts, though it is strongly recommended.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: In New Hampshire, what is the minimum age at which you may practice driving a non-commercial vehicle when accompanied by a licensed parent, guardian, or adult age 25 or older?
options: a:15 years of age.,b:16 years of age.,c:15 1/2 years of age.
note: New Hampshire does not issue a learner's permit. A resident may practice driving once they reach 15 1/2 years of age, provided they carry proof of age and are supervised in the front seat by a licensed parent, guardian, or adult age 25 or older.

question: Drowsy drivers:
options: a:Can stay alert by opening a window and turning up the radio.,b:Can drive so poorly they may appear to be drunk.,c:Should drink strong coffee to remain alert.
note: Drowsy driving can slow your reaction time, impair judgment, and cause you to drift from your lane, making your driving resemble that of an impaired driver. Tricks like opening a window, turning up the radio, or drinking coffee do not reliably keep you alert; the only safe solution is to rest before driving.

question: If you must stop along the road at night, what should you do with your lights?
options: a:Leave your low-beam headlights on (and use emergency flashers),b:Turn off all your lights,c:Use only your parking lights
note: If you must stop along the road at night, turn on your emergency flashers and keep your low-beam headlights on so other drivers can see you clearly. Turning off all lights or using only parking lights makes your vehicle much harder to see and increases the risk of a collision.

question: When driving in fog you should use:
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:Parking lights.,c:High beam headlights.
note: Use low beam headlights in fog, rain, or snow so you are better able to see and be seen.

question: When should you increase your following distance?
options: a:When behind a large vehicle that blocks your view or in bad weather.,b:Only when exiting an expressway.,c:Only when following a motorcycle.
note: Increase following distance in many situations: large vehicles that block vision, bad weather, heavy traffic, or if tailgated.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you're stopped in line at a stop sign and there is no cross traffic after vehicles ahead have passed, what must you do?
options: a:Stop again at the stop sign or stop line before proceeding.,b:Proceed without stopping because the way is clear.,c:Slowly roll past the stop sign.
note: You must always come to a complete stop at the stop sign and yield before proceeding, even if vehicles ahead have moved.

question: Many crashes are caused by drivers who:
options: a:Travel too fast for the conditions.,b:Constantly check their mirrors.,c:Yield the right-of-way.
note: Driving too quickly for road or weather conditions is a common factor in crashes.

question: If an oncoming driver fails to dim high beams, where should you direct your gaze?
options: a:Toward the right side of the road.,b:At the lights of the approaching vehicle.,c:Toward the left side of the road.
note: Glance to the right side of the road to avoid being blinded while keeping enough sight to stay on course.

question: Which statement best defines defensive driving?
options: a:Defensive driving means identifying dangerous situations and taking action to avoid accidents.,b:Defensive driving means defending yourself by getting ahead of bad drivers in traffic.,c:Defensive driving means following the vehicle ahead of you at a close distance.
note: Defensive driving is recognizing hazards early and taking action to avoid collisions, reducing conflicts with aggressive or inattentive road users.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which steps should you take when changing lanes on a highway?
options: a:Signal, check rearview and side mirrors, then glance over your shoulder to check blind spots.,b:Only signal if there is visible traffic behind you.,c:Just check your mirrors and change lanes quickly.
note: When changing lanes, always signal first to communicate your intention, then check your mirrors and quickly glance over your shoulder to make sure your blind spot is clear before moving over.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following has authority over the others and must be obeyed first?
options: a:A steady red light,b:A police officer,c:A stop sign
note: Directions given by a police officer or other authorized traffic officer take precedence over traffic signals, signs, or pavement markings.

question: Which of the following is a common sign of a drunk driver?
options: a:Weaving between lanes and making sudden, jerky movements.,b:Always driving faster than traffic.,c:Consistently maintaining perfect lane position.
note: A common sign of a drunk or impaired driver is weaving within or between lanes, drifting, or making sudden, jerky movements. Impaired drivers often have poor lane control and inconsistent speed.

question: Alcoholic beverages can affect you by:
options: a:Slowing your reaction time.,b:Giving you increased, accurate confidence.,c:Improving thinking ability.
note: Alcohol impairs reaction time, judgment, balance, and vision while giving false confidence.

question: What do work zone (orange) signs indicate?
options: a:Less-than-ideal driving conditions and that construction or maintenance is present.,b:That it is summer and roads are busier.,c:You must immediately stop and back up.
note: Orange work zone signs warn drivers of road work; slow down and be extra cautious.

question: When approaching a railroad crossing that has no gates or flashing lights, you should:
options: a:Prepare to yield to any train that may be approaching.,b:Cross the tracks immediately and as quickly as possible.,c:Always stop before crossing no matter what.
note: If there are no active signals, be prepared to yield and only cross when there is room for your entire vehicle on the other side and you are sure no trains are coming.

question: On a divided multilane highway when you hear or see an emergency vehicle, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down, move to provide a clear path, and stop.,b:Disregard the signal if other lanes are available.,c:Stop as quickly as possible wherever you are.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches, slow down and make a clear path by moving and stopping when safe; do not try to outdrive the vehicle.

question: What should you do when approaching a railroad crossing without signals?
options: a:Slow down and be prepared to stop.,b:Always come to a complete stop.,c:Assume there will always be signals.
note: At an un-signaled railroad crossing slow down, look and listen for trains, and be prepared to stop if a train is approaching.

question: In foggy conditions you should:
options: a:Drive cautiously, reduce your speed, and use low-beam headlights.,b:Use your high beams to see farther ahead.,c:Use parking lights only.
note: Fog reduces visibility; use low beams (and fog lights if equipped), slow down, and increase following distance.

question: When approaching a stopped school bus on the opposite side of a divided highway, what must drivers do?
options: a:May continue driving if the highway is divided.,b:Must stop until the bus begins moving.,c:Must stop until the stop arm is lifted regardless of division.
note: If the highway is divided by a median or barrier, drivers on the opposite side may continue; otherwise all lanes must stop for a stopped school bus with its signals activated.

question: How does the type of alcoholic drink affect impairment?
options: a:The effect on reflexes and judgment depends on blood alcohol level, not drink type.,b:Beer impairs less than wine.,c:Wine impairs less than beer.
note: Impairment depends on the amount of alcohol in the bloodstream, not whether it comes from beer, wine, or spirits.

question: If you are driving so slowly that traffic is backing up behind you on a two-lane, two-way road, you should:
options: a:Pull off to the right side of the road and let traffic pass.,b:Decrease your speed further.,c:Refuse to let other cars pass your vehicle.
note: Driving significantly slower than the flow of traffic is hazardous. On a two-lane road you must pull off and let vehicles pass when it is safe to do so.

question: What does a single dashed white line between lanes of traffic mean?
options: a:Drivers may pass or change lanes when it is safe to do so.,b:Traffic in the lanes moves in opposite directions.,c:Drivers may not pass in this area.
note: Dashed white lines separate lanes going in the same direction and may be crossed to pass or change lanes when it is safe.

question: Alcohol consumption commonly causes:
options: a:Loss of concentration.,b:Only poor coordination.,c:Only slower judgment.
note: Even small amounts of alcohol impair vision, concentration, judgment, and coordination.

question: A good defensive driver:
options: a:Always drives slowly.,b:Maintains a constant speed at all times.,c:Anticipates and watches for other drivers' actions.
note: Defensive driving means constantly scanning the road, anticipating what other drivers, pedestrians, and cyclists might do, and being ready to react safely. It is not about always driving slowly or keeping the same speed; it is about adjusting speed and position to conditions and potential hazards.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left onto a one-way street, you should complete the turn into:
options: a:The lane closest to your previous lane.,b:The right lane of the one-way street.,c:Either lane of the one-way street.
note: Turn from the lane nearest the direction you are traveling into the lane nearest the direction you want to go on the one-way street.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a four-way stop, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The vehicle that arrived first.,b:The vehicle that arrived last.,c:A vehicle may proceed without stopping.
note: At a four-way stop the driver who arrived first should proceed first. If two arrive simultaneously, the driver on the left yields to the driver on the right.

question: When backing a vehicle, you should:
options: a:Turn and look through the rear window while backing rather than relying only on mirrors.,b:Rely only on your mirrors, c:Open your door to see if it is safe to proceed.
note: When reversing, turn and look over your shoulder through the rear window; do not depend solely on mirrors or sensors.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing another vehicle, what should you do first?
options: a:Check mirrors and blind spots, signal, then pass when safe.,b:Honk at the vehicle three times to warn them.,c:Re-enter your lane within 10 feet of the passed vehicle.
note: Check mirrors and blind spots, signal your intent, pass safely, then return to the lane when you can see the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.

question: When parking downhill on a two-way street, how should you position your front wheels?
options: a:Turn the wheels to the right toward the curb.,b:Keep the wheels straight ahead.,c:Turn the wheels to the left away from the curb.
note: When parked downhill on a two-way street, turn front wheels toward the curb so the vehicle will roll into the curb rather than into traffic if it moves.

question: Which statement about passing a motorcycle is correct?
options: a:The driver of a passenger vehicle must change lanes completely when passing a motorcycle.,b:It is okay for other vehicles to follow motorcycles closely.,c:A motorcycle with two people is always more balanced than one with a single rider.
note: Motorcycles are entitled to a full lane, just like any other vehicle. When passing, you must move completely into the adjacent lane and give them the same or more space you would give a car. Never crowd or share a lane with a motorcycle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your exit on a freeway, what should you do?
options: a:Continue to the next exit and leave there.,b:Pull onto the shoulder and back up to the exit.,c:Make a U-turn across the median.
note: If you miss an exit, drive to the next one; do not stop, back up, or cross the median on the freeway.

question: If another vehicle is tailgating you, what should you do first if there is an open lane to your right?
options: a:If there is not an open lane to your right, wait until the way is clear ahead and reduce your speed slowly to encourage the tailgater to pass.,b:Move over to the right, if there is an open lane to your right.,c:Never slow down abruptly.
note: If someone is tailgating, move over to the right when it is safe to let them pass. If no lane is available, reduce speed gradually to encourage them to go around; avoid sudden braking.

question: Drivers who have been drinking before getting behind the wheel:
options: a:Do not have sufficient control over their bodies and minds or the vehicles being driven.,b:Are always aware of the risks they are taking.,c:Are better drivers because they are more careful than sober drivers.
note: Alcohol impairs judgment, vision, reaction time, and coordination; it is never safe to drive after drinking.

question: A leaking exhaust system can produce which dangerous effect?
options: a:Make you drowsy while driving and expose you to toxic fumes.,b:Require more frequent oil changes.,c:Reduce engine overheating only.
note: Leaky exhaust can let toxic gases into the vehicle, causing drowsiness, unconsciousness, or death in short order.

question: Which statement about driving on wet roadways is true?
options: a:The faster you drive, the less effective your tires are at clearing water.,b:Water does not affect cars with good tires.,c:Deep water is less dangerous than shallow water.
note: At higher speeds tires may lose contact with the road surface and the vehicle can hydroplane.

question: What does a single broken white line down the center of a multi-lane road indicate?
options: a:Lanes are moving in the same direction and drivers may change lanes when safe.,b:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and passing is prohibited.,c:Lanes are moving in the same direction and passing is never allowed.
note: Broken white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction; you may change lanes when safe to do so.

question: If an emergency vehicle is approaching with lights and siren, you must:
options: a:Only pull over if the emergency vehicle is behind you.,b:Continue driving if you are going faster than the emergency vehicle.,c:Pull over to the right edge of the road and stop
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches using lights and siren, you must yield the right-of-way by pulling over to the right edge of the road and stopping, if possible. Stay stopped until the emergency vehicle has passed, unless a police officer directs you otherwise.

question: How can you avoid alcohol-related crashes?
options: a:Say "No thanks" if you are offered a ride by someone who has been drinking.,b:Rely on coffee to sober up.,c:Decide before you start drinking that you will not drive.
note: The safest way to avoid an alcohol-related crash is to plan ahead and decide before you start drinking that you will not drive. Arrange a sober driver, use public transportation, or avoid drinking if you must drive. Once you have been drinking, your judgment is impaired and you are more likely to make unsafe decisions about driving.

question: A flashing yellow traffic signal indicates you should:
options: a:Come to a complete stop.,b:Slow down and proceed with caution.,c:Turn on your headlights.
note: A flashing yellow signal means caution. You do not have to stop, but you must slow down, look carefully for other traffic, pedestrians, or hazards, and proceed only when it is safe.

question: If you are involved in a crash and your vehicle is blocking traffic, you should:
options: a:Move your vehicle off the traveled portion of the roadway,b:Wait for police before moving your vehicle.,c:Not move your vehicle under any circumstances.
note: After a minor crash, if no one is seriously injured and the vehicles can be moved, you should move them out of the traffic lane to a safe location. This helps prevent additional crashes. You must still exchange information and render aid if needed, and you must not leave the scene.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a \No stopping\" sign generally allow you to do?"
options: a:Stop briefly to discharge passengers.,b:Stop to unload packages at any time.,c:Stop only to obey a traffic signal
note: A No Stopping sign means you may not stop your vehicle on that part of the roadway except when required to obey a traffic signal, sign, or police officer, or to avoid a conflict with other traffic. You may not stop there just to pick up or drop off people or goods.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What greatly increases stopping distances and crash severity?
options: a:Slow speeds.,b:Night driving.,c:High speeds.
note: The faster you drive, the longer it takes to stop and the harder you hit in a crash. High speeds greatly increase stopping distance and the force of impact, making collisions more severe.

question: Which of the following is true about sudden changes in weather and driving?
options: a:A sudden change in weather calls for an adjustment in your driving.,b:You should always slow down in rain and fog.,c:Be particularly aware of vehicles behind you only in inclement weather.
note: When weather changes suddenly—such as rain, fog, snow, or strong wind—you must adjust your driving. This usually means slowing down, increasing following distance, and being especially alert to traffic around you, including vehicles behind you.

question: What shape/color denotes a slow-moving vehicle emblem?
options: a:A circular green sign.,b:A reflective orange triangle.,c:A rectangular red sign.
note: The slow-moving vehicle emblem is a reflective orange triangle with a red border. It is used on vehicles that typically travel 25 mph or less, warning faster traffic to use extra caution and be prepared to slow down.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Driving significantly below the normal flow of traffic is:
options: a:Illegal in many situations because it can impede traffic.,b:Safe.,c:Smart.
note: Driving much slower than the normal flow of traffic can be dangerous because it forces other drivers to brake or change lanes suddenly. In many states, you must not drive so slowly that you block or impede normal traffic, except when necessary for safety or to comply with the law.

question: If another driver cuts you off, what's the safest response?
options: a:Pull next to them and yell.,b:Let it go and continue driving safely.,c:Flash your high beams at them.
note: If another driver cuts you off, the safest response is to stay calm, avoid eye contact or gestures, and continue driving defensively. Reacting aggressively, such as yelling or flashing high beams, can escalate the situation and increase the risk of a crash.

question: When you encounter a sign saying “Reduced speed, 35 mph,” what does it mean?
options: a:The new 35 mph speed limit begins at that sign.,b:You have plenty of distance before the reduced zone starts.,c:The reduced speed begins at the next sign.
note: A sign that says “Reduced speed, 35 mph” means the new 35 mph speed limit applies starting at that sign. You should slow down before reaching the sign so that you are already at or below 35 mph when you pass it.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When driving in traffic, what speed strategy is safest?
options: a:Drive faster than the flow to avoid being hit,b:Drive with the flow of traffic within the posted limits.,c:Drive significantly slower than other vehicles.
note: The safest strategy is to drive with the flow of traffic while staying within the posted speed limit. Large speed differences—either much faster or much slower than other vehicles—increase the chance of conflicts and collisions.

question: Your vehicle's brake lights inform other drivers that you:
options: a:Have your emergency brake on.,b:Are making a turn.,c:Are slowing down or stopping.
note: Brake lights are the red lights at the rear of your vehicle that come on when you press the brake pedal. They warn drivers behind you that you are slowing down or stopping so they can react in time and avoid a rear-end collision.

question: Which factors influence alcohol's effects on a person?
options: a:Only the amount of alcohol consumed.,b:Only the person's tolerance level.,c:Amount of food in the stomach.
note: Alcohol affects people differently based on several factors, including how much and how quickly they drink, their body weight, sex, and how much food is in the stomach. Food slows the absorption of alcohol into the bloodstream, which can reduce how quickly impairment occurs, but it does not prevent impairment if you keep drinking.

question: At light rail intersections, what should you always do?
options: a:Drive around lowered crossing gates if no train is visible.,b:Assume trains will stop for you.,c:Pay attention and obey all signs, signals, and gates at the crossing.
note: At light rail or train intersections, you must stay alert: obey all signs and signals, look and listen for trains in both directions, and be prepared to stop. Never drive around lowered gates or assume a train will stop for you; trains take a long distance to stop and always have the right-of-way.

question: If you approach a railroad crossing with flashing warning lights, you should:
options: a:Stop no closer than 15 feet from the nearest rail and look for a train.,b:Slow down and look for a train before crossing.,c:Proceed only if the lights are not flashing and the gates (if any) are fully raised.
note: Flashing lights at a railroad crossing mean a train is approaching. You must stop before the tracks, no closer than 15 feet from the nearest rail, and wait until the train has passed and the lights stop flashing before you proceed. Never try to beat a train through the crossing.

question: When parking uphill next to a curb, you should set the parking brake and:
options: a:Keep the front tires straight ahead.,b:Turn your steering wheel away from the curb.,c:Keep the rear tires against the curb.
note: When parking uphill next to a curb, turn your front wheels away from the curb and set the parking brake. If the vehicle rolls, the front tire will touch the curb and help stop the car from rolling into traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If the traffic light changes from green to yellow as you approach an intersection, you should:
options: a:Brake sharply to stop immediately in the center of the intersection.,b:Be prepared to stop safely.,c:Speed up to beat the red light.
note: A steady yellow light means the signal is about to turn red. You should slow down and be prepared to stop before the intersection if you can do so safely. Do not speed up to beat the red, and do not brake so hard that you risk being hit from behind or stopping in the middle of the intersection.

question: Passing is prohibited within how many feet of a railroad crossing?
options: a:200 feet,b:500 feet,c:100 feet
note: Passing is not allowed within 100 feet of a railroad crossing. This keeps you from moving into the oncoming lane where your view of trains and other traffic may be blocked and where other drivers may not expect a passing vehicle near the tracks.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you are approaching a heavy truck from behind while going uphill, which is true?
options: a:You may not be able to legally pass the truck.,b:You may not be able to safely pass the truck.,c:The truck may be traveling at a speed slower than the posted speed limit.
note: Heavy trucks often slow down on upgrades, but the key safety issue is whether you can pass them safely. On hills your view of oncoming traffic is often limited, and your vehicle may not have enough power to pass quickly. If you cannot see far enough ahead or complete the pass without exceeding the speed limit or cutting back too closely, you may not be able to safely pass the truck and should stay behind until it is clearly safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How close may you legally follow a fire truck that is responding to an emergency?
options: a:You may follow as close as 750 feet.,b:You may follow as close as one block.,c:You must not follow closer than 500 feet.
note: You must not follow an emergency vehicle that is responding to a call closer than 500 feet. This space lets the emergency vehicle maneuver freely and prevents you from interfering with its response. Never try to use an emergency vehicle to clear traffic for you or follow it into an emergency scene.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Unless posted otherwise, what is the maximum speed limit in a business district?
options: a:30 mph.,b:55 mph.,c:40 mph.
note: In many states, the default speed limit in a business district is 30 mph when no other limit is posted. Always watch for and obey posted signs, because local laws can set a lower or higher limit for specific streets.

question: How do you check your blind spot when changing lanes to the left?
options: a:Rely only on your side mirror.,b:Glance over your right shoulder.,c:Glance over your left shoulder.
note: To check your blind spot when moving left, quickly glance over your left shoulder after checking your mirrors. This brief head check lets you see the area your mirrors cannot cover and helps ensure no vehicle is beside you before you change lanes.

question: What is your blind spot?
options: a:The area you see in your rearview mirror.,b:An area you cannot see without moving your head.,c:The area directly behind your vehicle that's visible without turning.
note: Blind spots are areas around your vehicle that you cannot see in your mirrors alone. To see into these areas, you must briefly turn your head and look over your shoulder before changing lanes or merging.

question: When meeting a car with high beams on that blind you, what should you do?
options: a:Look toward the right edge of the road until the vehicle passes.,b:Speed up to get past the glare quickly.,c:Use your bright lights until they dim theirs.
note: When oncoming high beams blind you, shift your gaze to the right edge of your lane and use the road edge or lane line as a guide. This reduces glare while still letting you stay in your lane safely until the other vehicle passes.

question: What is the safe method for crossing a railroad track?
options: a:Cross quickly if a train appears to be approaching.,b:Look both ways only if the red light is flashing.,c:Look and listen both ways before crossing and obey all signals and gates.
note: Before crossing railroad tracks, slow down, look and listen carefully in both directions, and be prepared to stop. Cross only when you are sure no train is coming and there is enough space to clear the tracks completely without stopping on them.

question: Before entering a roundabout you must slow down and yield to whom?
options: a:Vehicles, bicyclists, and pedestrians already in or entering the roundabout.,b:Only bicyclists.,c:Only vehicles in the roundabout.
note: Before entering a roundabout, slow down and yield to traffic already in the circle, as well as to pedestrians and bicyclists in crosswalks. Vehicles inside the roundabout have the right-of-way, so wait for a safe gap before entering.

question: Which of these is NOT an effect of drinking?
options: a:Your reflexes and reaction time slow down.,b:You are less alert.,c:Your judgment of speed and distance becomes more accurate.
note: Alcohol slows your reflexes, reduces alertness, and makes your judgment of speed and distance worse, not better. Because your ability to judge how fast things are moving and how far away they are becomes less accurate, you are more likely to misjudge gaps, stopping distances, and the actions of other road users.

question: If stopped at a railroad crossing with multiple tracks, when should you proceed?
options: a:Wait until you have a clear view of all tracks before moving.,b:Stop on the first track and then creep forward to check the next.,c:Proceed as soon as the first train passes.
note: At a crossing with more than one track, a second train can come from either direction on another track. After the first train passes, wait until you can clearly see down all tracks in both directions and are sure no other train is coming before you proceed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you return to your lane after passing another vehicle?
options: a:When the other vehicle signals you to return.,b:When you can see the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.,c:When you are directly next to the vehicle.
note: After passing, you should not move back into your original lane until you can see the entire front of the vehicle you passed in your rearview mirror and have enough space to return safely. This ensures you do not cut off the other driver and that you have completed the pass.

question: When should you always use your turn signal?
options: a:Only when turning left.,b:Only when other traffic is present.,c:Whenever you change lanes, turn, or enter/leave traffic.
note: You must always signal before turning, changing lanes, entering or leaving a freeway, pulling away from a curb, or entering traffic from a driveway, alley, or parking space. Signaling lets other road users know your intentions so they can adjust safely, even if you think no one else is around.

question: If the driver ahead is distracted (one hand and talking), how should you respond?
options: a:Cut in front of them to avoid being behind a distracted driver.,b:Follow their example and drive similarly.,c:Give the vehicle extra space because its driver has a reduced safety margin.
note: A distracted driver is more likely to react slowly, drift in their lane, or miss hazards. By giving them extra space, you create a larger safety margin so that if they make a sudden or unsafe move, you have more time and room to respond.

question: If your vehicle lacks ABS and you need to stop quickly, what should you do?
options: a:Lightly tap the brakes.,b:Hold down the brake pedal steady.,c:Firmly pump the brakes.
note: For vehicles without ABS, you should apply firm pressure and pump the brakes to avoid wheel lockup. Pumping lets the tires briefly regain traction between brake applications so you can slow quickly while still being able to steer around hazards.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you approach a steady red traffic light you must:
options: a:Come to a complete stop.,b:Drive through if there is no crossing traffic.,c:Stop only if a police officer is nearby.
note: A steady red light always means stop before the crosswalk or stop line and remain stopped until the light turns green or you are allowed to turn right (or left on a one‑way onto a one‑way) after stopping and yielding, if not prohibited by signs and if it is safe.

question: How often must motor vehicles be inspected in New Hampshire?
options: a:Once every four years.,b:Once every two years.,c:Once a year during the owner's birth month.
note: In New Hampshire, most registered vehicles must be inspected every year during the month of the registered owner’s birthday at an official inspection station. This ensures the vehicle meets safety and, when applicable, emissions standards on a yearly basis.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You must stop at an intersection when you see which signal?
options: a:A steady yellow light.,b:A yellow arrow.,c:A flashing red light.
note: A flashing red light means you must come to a complete stop, just as you would at a stop sign. Stop at the stop line or before the crosswalk, yield to pedestrians and other traffic, and proceed only when it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should drivers treat a flashing red traffic light?
options: a:Continue because you have the right-of-way.,b:As a stop sign — stop,c:Drive through if no other cars are present.
note: A flashing red light is treated exactly like a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, check for traffic and pedestrians, yield as necessary, and then proceed only when the way is clear and it is safe.

question: Who is required by law to wear a seat belt in a moving vehicle?
options: a:Anyone under the age of 18.,b:All occupants, including the driver, regardless of age.,c:Only the driver.
note: In New Hampshire, anyone under the age of 18 is required by law to wear a seat belt (or be properly secured in a child safety seat). New Hampshire is the only U.S. state that does not legally require adults (18 and older) to wear seat belts, though it is strongly recommended for safety.

question: Which of the following is true about crosswalks?
options: a:They are always indicated by vertical pavement markings only.,b:They exist whether or not they are marked,c:They are always marked by horizontal pavement markings.
note: A crosswalk is the portion of the roadway set aside for pedestrian crossing. It can be marked with painted lines or unmarked at an intersection where sidewalks meet. Drivers must yield to pedestrians in both marked and unmarked crosswalks, so you must be prepared to stop even when you do not see painted lines.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After passing another vehicle on a two-lane road you should:
options: a:Return to the driving lane when there is enough room between you and the passed vehicle.,b:Remain in the left lane if you intend to turn left.,c:Return immediately to the right side of the roadway.
note: After passing, you should not cut back in too soon. Wait until you can see the front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror and there is a safe gap before returning to your lane. This ensures you do not force the other driver to slow or brake suddenly and keeps a safe following distance behind you.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a narrow road where you meet an oncoming vehicle, you must:
options: a:Allow the oncoming vehicle at least one-half of the main-traveled portion of the road.,b:Pull completely off the road and stop.,c:Demand the other vehicle pull over to make room.
note: On a narrow road, both drivers must cooperate so each vehicle has enough room to pass safely. You must allow the oncoming vehicle at least one-half of the main-traveled portion of the road. Slow down, keep as far to the right as is safe, and be prepared to stop if necessary so both vehicles can pass without leaving the roadway.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A driver may legally pass another vehicle on the right when:
options: a:It requires driving off the pavement.,b:On a narrow bridge.,c:The vehicle ahead is waiting to turn left and there is an available passing lane.
note: You may pass on the right only when it can be done safely and without leaving the paved roadway. A common legal situation is when the vehicle ahead is stopped or slowing to turn left and there is a clearly marked lane on the right for through traffic. You must never drive off the pavement or onto the shoulder to pass.

question: How is drinking alcohol and driving characterized in terms of traffic safety?
options: a:A minor traffic safety problem.,b:Safe if you have only had a few drinks.,c:A serious traffic safety problem.
note: Driving after drinking alcohol is always a serious traffic safety problem because alcohol slows your reaction time, reduces coordination, and impairs judgment. Even small amounts can affect your ability to drive safely and greatly increase your risk of a crash.

question: Traffic signs and pavement markings must be:
options: a:Considered mere suggestions.,b:Followed only when other traffic is present,c:Always obeyed.
note: Traffic signs, signals, and pavement markings are legal controls, not suggestions. They must always be obeyed because they assign right‑of‑way, control speed, and warn of hazards, helping prevent collisions and keep traffic moving safely.

question: Where are roads more likely to freeze first?
options: a:On bridges and overpasses.,b:Only on hills or curves.,c:In shaded areas such as under trees or near buildings.
note: Roads freeze sooner and stay icy longer where the surface gets less sunlight, such as in shaded areas under trees, near buildings, or in cuts through hills. These spots stay colder, so ice forms there first and melts last. Bridges and overpasses are also common early‑freezing locations because cold air surrounds them.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Into which lane should you turn when making a turn?
options: a:Into any lane available regardless of direction.,b:Into the lane farthest from your direction of travel.,c:Into the first available legal lane in the direction you're traveling.
note: When turning, you must enter the first legal lane going in your direction of travel. This keeps you from cutting across multiple lanes, reduces the chance of sideswipe or head‑on crashes, and makes your path more predictable to other drivers.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a street from a driveway, what must you do?
options: a:Drive slowly and expect others to get out of your way.,b:Honk to warn approaching vehicles and proceed.,c:Stop before the sidewalk and proceed only when no pedestrians or vehicles are approaching.
note: When entering a street from a driveway or alley, you must stop before crossing the sidewalk area, look for and yield to pedestrians, then yield to vehicles on the road. Only proceed when it is safe and clear in all directions.

question: When you hear a fire engine's siren behind you, you must:
options: a:Drive with your hazard flashers on.,b:Slow down until it passes,c:Pull over to the side of the road and stop.
note: When you see or hear an emergency vehicle using its siren and/or flashing lights, you must pull as close as safely possible to the right side of the road and stop until the vehicle has passed. This creates a clear path so the emergency vehicle can move quickly and safely. Do not stop in an intersection; clear the intersection first, then pull over.

question: Smoking or preparing to smoke while driving is:
options: a:Not affecting driving abilities.,b:Helpful to maintain driver alertness.,c:A distracting activity.
note: Smoking or preparing to smoke while driving is a distraction because it takes at least one hand off the wheel and can draw your eyes and attention away from the road. Dropped ashes or a lit cigarette can cause sudden, unsafe reactions. Any activity that interferes with full control of the vehicle and attention to driving increases crash risk.

question: Which of these is not a factor in stopping distance?
options: a:Braking distance.,b:Steering ability.,c:Reaction distance.
note: Total stopping distance is the distance your vehicle travels from the moment you see a hazard until you come to a complete stop. It includes perception distance (seeing the hazard), reaction distance (moving your foot to the brake), and braking distance (while the brakes slow the car). Steering ability does not change how far it takes to stop; it affects how you can maneuver, not your stopping distance.

question: To help avoid fatigue on a long trip it is a good idea to:
options: a:Drive with one eye open at a time.,b:Do arm exercises every hour.,c:Stop and rest every two hours.
note: On long trips, fatigue reduces your alertness and slows your reactions. To help avoid fatigue, plan to stop every couple of hours to rest, stretch, and move around. If you feel drowsy, get off the road and rest or change drivers. Tricks like opening a window or doing exercises while driving are not safe or effective substitutes for real rest.

question: Lanes moving in the same direction are divided by which color lines?
options: a:Yellow lines.,b:Red lines.,c:White lines.
note: White lines separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction, such as on multi-lane city streets or freeways. Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. Knowing this helps you understand when you are allowed to change lanes and what direction other vehicles around you are traveling.

question: What is the most common color of warning signs?
options: a:Green.,b:Red.,c:Yellow with black markings.
note: Warning signs are typically diamond-shaped and yellow with black symbols or words. They alert you to upcoming hazards or changes in road conditions so you can slow down and prepare.

question: A flashing yellow traffic signal tells drivers to:
options: a:Expect merging traffic only.,b:Stop for pedestrians.,c:Proceed with caution.
note: A flashing yellow signal means you must slow down and proceed with caution. You do not have to stop, but you must be prepared to yield to pedestrians and other traffic already in the intersection.

question: Approximately how far might a fully loaded tractor-trailer need to stop from 55 mph?
options: a:About 50 feet.,b:About 125 feet.,c:About 400 feet.
note: A fully loaded tractor‑trailer needs much more distance to stop than a passenger car. At about 55 mph, it can take roughly 400 feet or more to come to a complete stop, so you should avoid cutting closely in front of large trucks.

question: What is a 'No zone'?
options: a:A one-way traffic area,b:A designated no passing zone,c:The blind spot area around a large commercial vehicle.
note: The "No zone" is the large blind spot area around trucks and buses where the driver cannot see you in their mirrors. If you cannot see the truck driver’s mirrors, they likely cannot see you, so avoid staying in these areas.

question: When driving to an unfamiliar place, the best preparation is to:
options: a:Drive with only a general idea of where you are going.,b:Plan your route in advance.,c:Depend on road signs to find your way
note: Planning your route in advance reduces stress and distraction. Knowing where you are going before you drive lets you focus on traffic and road conditions instead of searching for turns or reading directions while driving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Signaling your intentions before turning or changing lanes is:
options: a:Required by law and a good driving habit.,b:Necessary only if other traffic is present.,c:Necessary only during the maneuver
note: Signaling is required by law before turning or changing lanes so other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians know what you plan to do. You must signal well in advance—typically at least 100 feet before turning on regular roads (and more at higher speeds)—and keep the signal on through the maneuver so others can react safely.

question: When is sounding your horn appropriate?
options: a:When you see a child who is about to run into the street.,b:Whenever you are passing a bicyclist.,c:While you are traveling through an intersection
note: Use your horn to warn others when there is a potential collision, such as when a child is about to run into the street or another driver is about to hit you. Do not use the horn unnecessarily, such as every time you pass a bicyclist or while simply driving through intersections, because that can startle others and create confusion.

question: When should you drive below the posted speed limit?
options: a:Only when you see a police car.,b:When entering a highway with other cars.,c:Whenever conditions such as weather or visibility make driving less than perfect.
note: The posted speed limit is the maximum speed allowed under ideal conditions, not a target speed. You must slow down below the limit whenever rain, snow, ice, fog, heavy traffic, or poor visibility make the posted speed unsafe so you can stop and react in time.

question: If two railroad tracks run next to each other, after one train passes you should:
options: a:Always stop before crossing even if no trains are visible.,b:Assume it is safe to proceed because one train has passed.,c:Look for another train approaching on the other track before proceeding.
note: At crossings with more than one track, one train can hide another that is approaching on the next track. After the first train passes, wait, look, and listen again for another train on any track before you proceed, and only cross when you are sure all tracks are clear.

question: What is the only effective way to lower your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Drink coffee to sober up quickly.,b:Exercise to reduce BAC.,c:Allow your body time to metabolize the alcohol.
note: Only time lowers your blood alcohol concentration because your liver must metabolize the alcohol. Coffee, exercise, cold showers, or other tricks may make you feel more awake but do not speed up how quickly alcohol leaves your system or make you safe to drive.

question: When parking uphill on a street with a curb, you should turn your front wheels:
options: a:Slightly to the right.,b:Sharply toward the curb.,c:Sharply away from the curb.
note: When you park facing uphill with a curb, turn the front wheels sharply away from the curb. If the vehicle rolls, the back of the front tire will touch the curb and stop the car from rolling into traffic.

question: On slippery roads, you should take turns and curves:
options: a:More quickly to clear the hazard faster.,b:At the same speed as usual.,c:More slowly than you would under normal conditions.
note: On slippery roads, reduce speed before entering turns and curves. Lower speed gives your tires more grip and reduces the chance of skidding or losing control.

question: What is your first action if your accelerator sticks while driving?
options: a:Shift to neutral and apply steady pressure to the brakes.,b:Reach down and attempt to pull it up.,c:Shift to park immediately.
note: If the accelerator sticks, keep your eyes on the road, shift to neutral, and apply steady pressure to the brakes. Then move safely off the road and turn off the engine. Do not reach down to pull the pedal up or shift to park while moving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If an intersection ahead is blocked by traffic you should:
options: a:Go slowly until the traffic ahead moves.,b:Stay out of the intersection until you can pass through without stopping.,c:Get as close as possible to the car in front of you.
note: You must not enter an intersection unless you can completely clear it. If traffic is stopped ahead, wait before the intersection so you do not block cross traffic when the light changes.

question: What is the most important rule for managing speed in curves?
options: a:Maintain the posted speed limit entering the curve and brake only in the sharpest part.,b:Accelerate gently before entering the curve.,c:Slow down before you enter the curve.
note: Slow down before you enter a curve, then maintain a safe, steady speed through it. Braking hard inside the curve can cause skids because your tires are already working to change direction.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What must you do when you come to an intersection with a flashing red light?
options: a:Slow down but do not stop.,b:Proceed without stopping if no other cars are present.,c:Come to a full stop and go only when it is safe.
note: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, check for traffic and pedestrians, yield the right-of-way as needed, and then proceed only when it is safe.

question: You may not park within how many feet of a crosswalk at an intersection?
options: a:20 feet.,b:10 feet.,c:30 feet.
note: You may not park within 20 feet of a crosswalk at an intersection. This space must be kept clear so drivers can see pedestrians entering the crosswalk and so pedestrians can see approaching traffic.

question: Turning onto a two-lane road marked by a broken yellow centerline tells you:
options: a:The road is under repair.,b:You are on a two-way road.,c:You are on a one-way road.
note: A broken yellow centerline separates traffic moving in opposite directions on a two-way road. You may cross a broken yellow line to pass when it is safe and legal to do so.

question: Guide signs that give directions and mileage information are usually what color?
options: a:Yellow,b:Red,c:Green
note: Guide or destination signs that show directions, routes, and distances are usually green with white lettering, helping drivers navigate to cities, streets, and exits.

question: When an oncoming vehicle is approaching at night, your headlights should be set to:
options: a:High-beam headlights,b:Off; use parking lights only,c:Low-beam headlights
note: When another vehicle is approaching at night, you must use low-beam headlights so you do not blind the other driver. High beams are only for use when there is no oncoming traffic and you are not closely following another vehicle.

question: If you need to slow on a slippery road, what should you do first?
options: a:Apply the parking brake.,b:Firmly apply your brakes.,c:Take your foot off the gas pedal.
note: On a slippery road, sudden braking can cause skids. First ease off the accelerator so the vehicle slows gradually using engine braking. If you need to slow more, then apply the brakes gently and steadily to maintain traction and control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an uncontrolled intersection you should:
options: a:Yield to vehicles approaching from the right and be prepared to stop.,b:Maintain your speed and proceed.,c:Always stop at the intersection.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection, no signs or signals assign right‑of‑way, so you must slow, be ready to stop, and yield to vehicles approaching from your right. Enter only when you are sure it is safe, even if you technically have the right‑of‑way.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto a freeway, what's usually best?
options: a:Turn on hazards until fully merged.,b:Accelerate on the ramp to match freeway traffic speed.,c:Proceed slowly and wait for a gap.
note: When entering a freeway, use the entrance ramp and acceleration lane to reach a speed that matches the flow of freeway traffic, then merge when there is a safe gap. Always yield to vehicles already on the freeway and avoid merging too slowly, which can create a hazard.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A steady red traffic signal requires you to:
options: a:Stop at the stop line, before the crosswalk, or at a point before entering the intersection where you can see cross traffic.,b:Stop only if pedestrians are present in the crosswalk.,c:Stop before entering the intersection, obeying any stop line or crosswalk markings.
note: A steady red light means you must come to a complete stop before entering the intersection. If there is a stop line, stop before the line. If there is a crosswalk, stop before entering the crosswalk. If there are no markings, stop at a point before the intersection where you can see cross traffic and proceed only when allowed and safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When two vehicles arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, who goes first?
options: a:The vehicle approaching from the left.,b:The vehicle whose driver honks first.,c:The vehicle approaching from the right.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection where two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. The vehicle approaching from the right has the right‑of‑way and may proceed first when it is safe.

question: Warning signs indicating upcoming hazards usually have what colors?
options: a:Black letters or symbols on a white background.,b:White letters or symbols on a blue background.,c:Black letters or symbols on a yellow background.
note: Warning signs that alert you to upcoming hazards are usually yellow with black symbols or lettering. Construction and maintenance warning signs are orange with black symbols or lettering. These colors help drivers quickly recognize that extra caution is needed.

question: If you leave your vehicle unattended you must:
options: a:Set the parking brake only.,b:Stop the engine, lock the ignition, remove the key, and set the parking brake.,c:Turn off the engine only.
note: When leaving a vehicle unattended you must stop the engine, lock the ignition, remove the key, and set the parking brake.

question: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in which situations?
options: a:Only when the pedestrian is on the same side of the road.,b:Drivers must yield to pedestrians in crosswalks—marked or unmarked—and must use due care to avoid hitting any pedestrian in the roadway.,c:Only in marked crosswalks.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in crosswalks, whether the crosswalk is marked or unmarked, and must use due care to avoid hitting any pedestrian in the roadway. Even if a pedestrian is crossing against a signal or acting carelessly, you are still required to slow or stop if necessary to avoid a collision.

question: When is a right turn on red prohibited?
options: a:Only when a pedestrian is present.,b:When a sign prohibits right on red or when a steady WALK signal is displayed for the crosswalk you would turn across.,c:When a vehicle is in the intersection on the opposite side.
note: You may generally turn right on red after stopping completely and yielding to traffic and pedestrians, unless a sign specifically prohibits a right turn on red. You must also remain stopped if a steady WALK signal is displayed for the crosswalk you would be turning across, because pedestrians have the right of way during that signal.

question: If you're involved in a collision, what should you do first?
options: a:Drive away if the damage is minor.,b:Stop immediately and assist the injured as needed.,c:Call your insurance company and then leave.
note: If you are involved in a collision, you must stop immediately at or near the scene. Check for injuries, call emergency services if needed, and give reasonable assistance without moving injured persons unless there is immediate danger. When it is safe, move vehicles out of traffic to prevent further crashes and exchange information with the other parties.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you see a Merging traffic sign on the freeway, what should you do?
options: a:Make room for entering vehicles by changing lanes if possible.,b:Always remain at your present speed.,c:Honk at incoming traffic to warn them.
note: On a freeway, a merging traffic sign warns that vehicles will be entering your lane from an on‑ramp. You should be prepared to adjust your speed and, if safe, change lanes to create space for them to merge smoothly. Never speed up to block merging vehicles or use your horn aggressively.

question: If you must drive in fog, use which headlights?
options: a:Parking lights,b:High-beam headlights,c:Low-beam headlights
note: In fog, always use low‑beam headlights. High beams reflect off the water droplets in the fog and shine back into your eyes, making it harder to see. Low beams (and fog lights if your vehicle has them) reduce glare and help you see the road and be seen by others.

question: A pennant-shaped traffic sign is used to indicate:
options: a:A speed limit.,b:A no passing zone.,c:A school zone.
note: A pennant‑shaped sign, which is a sideways triangle pointing to the right, marks the beginning of a no passing zone on two‑lane roads. It warns you that it is unsafe and illegal to pass other vehicles in that area, even if the way looks clear.

question: When driving near a motorcycle you must:
options: a:Allow the motorcycle to use only half a lane.,b:Allow the motorcycle to use a complete lane.,c:Drive on the shoulder beside the motorcycle.
note: Motorcycles are entitled to a full lane, just like any other motor vehicle. Do not crowd them or try to share the lane beside them. Give motorcycles extra space because they are less visible and need room to maneuver and avoid road hazards.

question: What must you do with your headlights when driving in rain?
options: a:Use parking lights only.,b:Use low beam headlights.,c:Use high beam headlights.
note: When driving in rain, use your low‑beam headlights so you can see the road and so other drivers can see you. High beams create more glare and can reflect off rain, reducing visibility. In many states, headlights are legally required whenever wipers are in use.

question: If your vehicle's turn signals are not working, how should you show other road users your intentions?
options: a:Use hand signals to indicate turns and lane changes.,b:Use your headlights.,c:Sound your horn instead.
note: If your electrical turn signals fail, you must use standard hand and arm signals to indicate turns and lane changes. This lets other drivers know your intentions and is required by law when signal lights are not working.

question: What is the purpose of an advisory speed sign attached to a curve warning sign?
options: a:To indicate a minimum legal speed.,b:To be ignored in rain or snow.,c:To recommend a safe speed for the curve which should be reduced in poor conditions.
note: An advisory speed sign on a curve warns of a recommended safe speed under ideal conditions, not a legal maximum or minimum. In rain, snow, or other poor conditions, you should slow down even more than the posted advisory speed.

question: If you are stopped by a police officer, you should:
options: a:Get your paperwork ready and then exit the vehicle to meet the officer.,b:Stay in your vehicle with your hands visible on the steering wheel and wait for the officer to approach.,c:Unbuckle your seat belt and lower your window before the officer reaches you.
note: When stopped by police, pull over safely, stay in the vehicle, keep your hands visible on the steering wheel, and wait for instructions. Do not exit or reach around for items unless the officer asks you to, as sudden movements can create safety concerns.

question: Which of these suggestions is least directly related to promoting safe night driving?
options: a:Carry a small flashlight in your vehicle.,b:Be aware that tinted windows reduce visibility at night.,c:Keep your windshield clean.
note: Safe night driving mainly depends on seeing and being seen: clean windows and mirrors, properly aimed and working headlights, and avoiding dark or heavily tinted glass that reduces visibility. A small flashlight can help in an emergency but does not directly improve how safely you drive at night.

question: When you see a blind pedestrian who is using a white cane or guide dog, you should:
options: a:Take the right-of-way,b:Slow down and be prepared to stop,c:Proceed normally without reducing speed.
note: Blind pedestrians using a white cane or guide dog have the right-of-way. You must slow down, be prepared to stop, and yield so they can cross safely. Never rush through or take the right-of-way from a visually impaired pedestrian.

question: On average, how many alcoholic drinks does the body eliminate in one hour?
options: a:About one drink per hour.,b:About three drinks per hour.,c:About two drinks per hour.
note: An average adult body can process about one standard drink per hour. A standard drink is roughly 12 oz of beer, 5 oz of wine, or 1.5 oz of 80‑proof liquor. Because many factors affect impairment—such as weight, sex, food, and tolerance—you can still be unsafe to drive even at or below this rate.

question: What is the No zone in relation to large trucks or buses?
options: a:A restricted audio volume area for vehicle stereos.,b:The blind spots around a truck or bus where the driver cannot see you.,c:A special speed zone around large vehicles.
note: The No‑Zone is the large blind‑spot area around trucks and buses where the driver cannot see you in their mirrors. These areas are along both sides, directly behind, and sometimes directly in front of the vehicle. If you stay in a No‑Zone, the driver may not know you are there, increasing the risk of a collision.

question: What happens when you take drugs along with alcohol?
options: a:The combined use increases the risk of causing a crash.,b:The combination is no more dangerous than alcohol alone.,c:The drugs lessen alcohol's effect on driving.
note: Combining alcohol with any drug—prescription, over‑the‑counter, or illegal—can greatly increase drowsiness, slow reaction time, and impair judgment more than either substance alone. This makes driving much more dangerous and significantly raises the risk of a crash.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a highway from an entrance ramp you should generally do what?
options: a:Enter slowly to avoid other vehicles.,b:Stop on the ramp then enter.,c:Use the acceleration lane to reach highway speed and merge with traffic.
note: When using a highway entrance ramp, use the acceleration lane to match the speed of traffic on the highway, then merge when there is a safe gap. Always yield to vehicles already on the highway; do not stop on the ramp unless traffic or signs require it.

question: If a transit vehicle signals to re-enter the main road after stopping, what must you do?
options: a:Honking to alert the driver.,b:Maintain speed and position.,c:Yield and allow it to safely re-enter.
note: When a transit vehicle signals to re‑enter the main road after a stop, you must yield and allow it to merge safely. Adjust your speed or change lanes if needed so the bus can rejoin traffic without forcing sudden braking or swerving.

question: What effect does even a small amount of alcohol have on driving-related abilities?
options: a:Only a blood alcohol level greater than the legal limit will reduce these abilities.,b:Even the smallest amount of alcohol can reduce concentration,c:Alcohol does not reduce these driving abilities.
note: Even small amounts of alcohol can slow your reactions and affect concentration, judgment, and perception. There is no completely safe amount of alcohol for driving; any drinking can reduce your ability to drive safely.

question: When must you stop at a railroad crossing?
options: a:You must stop when warning devices show a train is coming or when required by a sign or flagger.,b:You only need to stop if the gates are down.,c:You must stop when directed by a flagger or stop sign, or when warning devices or an approaching train indicate it is unsafe to cross.
note: You must stop at a railroad crossing when a stop sign, flagger, or other traffic control tells you to stop, and also when warning devices show a train is coming. This includes flashing red lights, lowered gates, a visible or clearly audible train, or a train so close it would be unsafe to cross.

question: When making a turn, you must do what to your speed?
options: a:Increase your speed.,b:Maintain or vary your speed at will.,c:Reduce your speed to maintain control.
note: Before and during a turn, you should slow down enough to stay in your lane and keep control of the vehicle. Enter the turn at a safe speed, then accelerate gently as you complete the turn if conditions allow.

question: If your vehicle begins to skid you should:
options: a:Overcorrect the steering.,b:Turn the steering wheel in the direction of the skid.,c:Turn the steering wheel into oncoming traffic.
note: If your vehicle begins to skid, ease off the accelerator and steer in the direction you want the front of the vehicle to go, which is generally the same direction the rear of the vehicle is skidding. This helps you straighten the vehicle and regain control without overcorrecting.

question: What should you do to avoid collisions with vehicles in your blind spots?
options: a:Honk your horn right before changing lanes.,b:Adjust your rearview mirrors every few minutes.,c:Turn your head and glance over your shoulder to check blind spots before changing lanes.
note: Every vehicle has blind spots that mirrors cannot show. Before changing lanes, quickly turn your head and look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move to be sure no vehicle is in your blind spot.

question: Compared to daytime driving, how is night driving different?
options: a:Less dangerous.,b:The same as daytime driving.,c:More dangerous because visibility is reduced.
note: Night driving is more dangerous because you cannot see as far or as clearly, glare from headlights can reduce your vision, and there are often more tired or impaired drivers on the road. You must slow down and be extra alert at night.

question: On long trips you can prevent drowsiness by:
options: a:Stopping at regular intervals for rest.,b:Turning on the car radio.,c:Slowing down.
note: Take regular breaks to rest and stretch during long trips to avoid drowsiness.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are moving from the right lane into the left lane on a multilane highway, what checks should you make?
options: a:Look in mirrors and over your left shoulder for traffic in the blind spot,b:Only look in the rearview mirror and then change lanes quickly.,c:Signal and assume the lane is clear without looking.
note: Before moving into the left lane, check your mirrors and then quickly look over your left shoulder to see the blind spot. Signal, make sure the lane is clear, and then change lanes smoothly. Never rely only on mirrors or your signal.

question: Which of the following substances can impair driving and lead to DUII charges?
options: a:Alcohol and other impairing drugs and medicines.,b:Only alcohol.,c:Only illegal drugs.
note: Driving under the influence laws apply to alcohol, illegal drugs, some prescription medicines, and other substances that impair your ability to drive safely. Any alcoholic drink—beer, wine, or liquor—can lead to a DUI if it impairs you or your blood alcohol level is over the legal limit.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On most roadways you should signal your intent to turn at least:
options: a:300 feet before the turn.,b:500 feet before the turn.,c:100 feet before the turn.
note: On most regular roads, you must signal at least 100 feet before you turn so other drivers and pedestrians have time to react. On higher-speed roads and highways, signal even earlier to give extra warning.

question: If you are in an accident and someone is injured, what should you do?
options: a:Do not move the injured unless necessary; keep them warm and provide first aid if able.,b:Move the injured immediately away from the scene.,c:Always leave injured people where they are without attempting aid.
note: In a crash with injuries, your first priorities are to prevent further harm and get medical help. Call emergency services, do not move injured people unless there is immediate danger (like fire or risk of another collision), keep them warm and calm, and provide basic first aid if you are able until professionals arrive.

question: If you start to feel tired while driving, what is the best action?
options: a:Stop driving and rest.,b:Have some coffee and keep driving.,c:Open the window and continue.
note: Drowsy driving greatly slows reaction time and decision‑making. Short‑term tricks like coffee or opening a window do not restore alertness enough to be safe. The safest choice when you feel tired is to stop driving, rest, or change drivers before continuing.

question: To reduce headlight glare from oncoming vehicles at night, where should you look?
options: a:Over your shoulder.,b:Straight at the oncoming headlights.,c:Toward the right side of the road ahead.
note: Bright oncoming headlights can temporarily blind you. Instead of looking directly at them, shift your gaze slightly to the right edge of your lane or the right side of the road ahead, using lane markings as a guide. This keeps you oriented while reducing glare.

question: Lack of sleep affects driving ability similar to which of these?
options: a:The effects of amphetamines.,b:The effects of anger.,c:The effects of alcohol on driving performance.
note: Driving while very tired can impair you in ways similar to alcohol: slower reactions, poor judgment, and drifting from your lane. Studies show that being awake for long periods can produce impairment comparable to driving with an illegal blood alcohol level, so you must treat fatigue as a serious safety risk.

question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning?
options: a:Brake hard when entering standing water.,b:Drive more quickly through shallow water.,c:Drive more slowly in wet conditions.
note: Hydroplaning happens when your tires ride on top of water instead of gripping the road, which is more likely at higher speeds. To reduce this risk, slow down in wet conditions, especially in standing water, and make smooth, gentle steering and braking inputs.

question: Which practice best helps ensure safety when backing your vehicle?
options: a:Honk just before shifting into reverse.,b:Check only the rearview mirrors.,c:Walk to the rear of the vehicle and check behind it before getting in.
note: Before backing, walk behind your vehicle to check for children, pets, or objects that may be in your blind spots. Mirrors alone cannot show everything directly behind you, so physically checking the area first is the safest practice.

question: Under normal conditions, what is the minimum following distance you should keep?
options: a:Three seconds.,b:One second.,c:Two seconds.
note: Keep at least a three-second following distance under normal conditions; increase this distance when conditions worsen.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A flashing red traffic signal requires you to:
options: a:Come to a complete stop, yield, and go only when safe.,b:Slow down at the light.,c:Merge to the right immediately.
note: A flashing red light means stop, yield to traffic and pedestrians, and proceed only when it is safe.

question: You may not legally park your vehicle in which of the following locations?
options: a:On a hill.,b:In a parking lot.,c:On a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane.
note: You may not park on a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane because these areas must remain clear for pedestrians and cyclists. When parking along a curb where it is allowed, you must park close and parallel to the curb, typically within about 12–18 inches depending on state law.

question: If you have a green light but pedestrians are crossing against the light, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up to pass in front of them.,b:Stop and let the pedestrians cross safely.,c:Honk to make them hurry.
note: Even if you have a green light, you must yield to pedestrians in the roadway, including those crossing against the signal. Slow down and stop if necessary so they can cross safely, and do not try to drive around or intimidate them.

question: When roads may be slippery you should:
options: a:Use cruise control to maintain speed.,b:Increase your following distance and reduce speed.,c:Always drive at the maximum speed limit.
note: On slippery roads you should slow down, increase your following distance, and avoid sudden steering, braking, or acceleration. Using cruise control on a slippery surface is unsafe because it can cause the wheels to spin and you may lose control. You should leave more space, not less, between you and the vehicle ahead so you have extra time to react.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing a slower vehicle on a two-lane, two-way road, you must:
options: a:Use the shoulder.,b:Not cross the centerline.,c:Use the lane belonging to oncoming traffic to complete the pass.
note: On a two-lane, two-way road, you normally must move into the lane used by oncoming traffic to pass a slower vehicle. Only do this when passing is legal (no solid yellow line on your side, no signs prohibiting passing) and when you have enough clear distance to complete the pass safely without interfering with oncoming traffic.

question: How should you regard railroad crossings?
options: a:Safe to cross in most cases.,b:Always potentially dangerous.,c:A safe place to park.
note: Railroad crossings are always potentially dangerous because trains are large, fast, and cannot stop quickly. You should always approach crossings with caution, look and listen for trains, and be prepared to stop even if warning devices are not activated.

question: Drivers who eat or drink while driving:
options: a:Are better drivers because they are not hungry.,b:Are more likely to have trouble staying in their lane and controlling the vehicle.,c:Make no driving errors.
note: Eating or drinking while driving takes at least one hand off the wheel and your attention away from the road. This increases the chance of drifting out of your lane, varying your speed unintentionally, and reacting too slowly to hazards. To drive safely, keep your focus and hands on driving tasks.

question: When approaching railroad tracks you should:
options: a:Never drive around a lowered gate.,b:Look, listen, slow down, and be prepared to stop.,c:Never speed up to try to beat a train.
note: When approaching railroad tracks, always slow down, look, and listen for trains, and be prepared to stop. Never try to drive around lowered gates or speed up to beat a train; trains are much faster and closer than they appear, and you must always yield the right-of-way to them.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If driving on a one-way street and an emergency vehicle using lights approaches, what must you do?
options: a:Speed up and exit the roadway.,b:Turn on your hazard flashers and keep going.,c:Drive toward the nearest roadside and stop.
note: On any roadway, including a one‑way street, you must yield to emergency vehicles using lights or siren. Move as close as you safely can to the nearest edge of the road (right or left on a one‑way) and stop until the emergency vehicle has passed.

question: In poor weather conditions, what should drivers do regarding following distance?
options: a:Decrease their following distance.,b:Maintain the same following distance as in dry conditions.,c:Increase their following distance.
note: In rain, snow, fog, or on icy roads, your stopping distance increases. To stay safe, leave more space between your vehicle and the one ahead so you have extra time and distance to react and stop smoothly.

question: Under which circumstance may you drive around lowered gates at a railroad crossing?
options: a:When the lights stop flashing.,b:When the train has passed.,c:Under no circumstances.
note: Lowered gates mean a train is approaching or nearby. It is illegal and extremely dangerous to drive around or under lowered railroad gates. You must wait until the gates are fully raised and signals indicate it is safe and legal to cross.

question: What does a broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line mean?
options: a:No passing is permitted in either direction.,b:Passing is permitted from the lane next to the solid line.,c:Passing is permitted from the lane next to the broken line.
note: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means only the traffic on the side with the broken line may pass, and only when it is safe. Traffic next to the solid yellow line must not cross it to pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you pass another vehicle by using the right shoulder?
options: a:When the car in front is driving too slowly.,b:Never.,c:When the car in front is turning.
note: Passing on the right shoulder is unsafe and generally illegal. You must stay on the paved travel lane when passing; do not drive off the roadway or onto the shoulder to go around another vehicle, even if it is slow or turning.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If waiting to turn left at a multilane intersection and opposing traffic blocks your view, what should you do?
options: a:Accelerate rapidly when the first lane clears.,b:Signal and rely on another driver to wave you through.,c:Wait until you can see all lanes you must cross before making the turn.
note: When turning left, you must not start your turn until you can clearly see that every lane you must cross is free of oncoming traffic, pedestrians, and other hazards. If large vehicles or multiple lanes block your view, wait behind the crosswalk or stop line until you have a clear line of sight. Never rely on other drivers waving you through or try to dart out quickly; you are responsible for making sure the turn is safe.

question: When driving near heavy trucks, what should other road users allow for?
options: a:The lower noise levels of large vehicles.,b:The decreased stopping distance of large vehicles.,c:The increased stopping distance required by large vehicles.
note: Large trucks and other heavy vehicles need a much longer distance to stop because of their size and weight. When driving near them, leave extra space in front of the truck, avoid cutting in too closely, and do not assume they can stop as quickly as a passenger car. Staying out of their blind spots and giving them room to brake helps prevent rear-end and sideswipe collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where should you NOT pass other vehicles?
options: a:On an expressway only.,b:Whenever the lane looks clear.,c:On a hill or curve.
note: Passing on a hill or curve is dangerous because your view of oncoming traffic is limited, and oncoming drivers may not see you in time. You should only pass where you have a clear, long view of the road ahead and where passing is permitted by signs and pavement markings. Never pass near intersections, railroad crossings, bridges, or anywhere your view is blocked.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Approaching a steady yellow traffic light you should:
options: a:Continue because you have the right-of-way.,b:Accelerate to avoid a red light.,c:Slow to a stop unless you are already in the intersection.
note: A steady yellow light means the signal is about to turn red. You must slow down and stop before the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are already in the intersection or so close that stopping suddenly would cause a crash, continue through carefully. Do not speed up to beat the red light, as this increases the risk of collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you see a steady green arrow at a signal, what may drivers do?
options: a:Stop before proceeding in the arrow's direction.,b:Merge into any lane regardless of direction.,c:Turn in the direction of the arrow after yielding to traffic and pedestrians already in the intersection.
note: A steady green arrow means you have a protected turn in the direction of the arrow.
