You may make the turn, but you must still yield to any vehicles, bicycles, or pedestrians already in the intersection. Use the correct turn lane, check for people in the crosswalk, and complete the turn only when the path is clear.

question: If your vehicle’s right wheels leave the pavement, what is the recommended action?
options: a:Slow down,b:Accelerate and steer back onto the road as fast as possible.,c:Stop quickly immediately.
note: If your right wheels drop off the pavement, keep a firm grip on the wheel, stay off the gas and brakes, and gradually slow down. Once you have the car under control and traffic is clear, gently steer back onto the pavement. Jerking the wheel or braking hard can cause you to lose control or skid.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When the driver behind you wants to pass, what is the correct action?
options: a:Slow down to allow room in front of your vehicle for the pass.,b:Maintain the same speed.,c:Speed up to prevent them from passing.
note: When someone wants to pass you, help them do it safely. Slightly reduce your speed to create more space in front of you so they can move back into the lane sooner. Never speed up to block a pass; that increases risk and can be illegal. Maintain a steady path and let them complete the maneuver.

question: When it starts to rain while you're driving, what is the correct action?
options: a:Slow down.,b:Maintain the maximum posted speed limit.,c:Drive faster than surrounding traffic.
note: When rain begins, the road becomes especially slippery as water mixes with oil and dirt. Reduce your speed, increase following distance, and turn on your headlights so you can see and be seen. If visibility or traction becomes too poor, safely pull off the road and wait for conditions to improve.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When exiting a highway, when should you begin to slow down?
options: a:Once you see a toll booth.,b:After you have moved into the exit lane.,c:On the main road just before the exit lane.
note: On a highway, stay at traffic speed until you reach the exit lane. Signal and move into the exit lane first, then begin to slow down to the posted exit or ramp speed. Slowing on the main travel lane before entering the exit lane can surprise drivers behind you and increase the risk of a rear‑end collision.

question: A steady yellow traffic light approaching an intersection tells you to:
options: a:Go.,b:Yield to other cars.,c:Slow down and prepare to stop.
note: A steady yellow light means the signal is about to turn red. You should slow down and prepare to stop before the intersection. Proceed only if you are so close that stopping safely is not possible; otherwise, entering on yellow risks being in the intersection when the light turns red.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which traffic light condition is equivalent to coming to a full stop, yielding, then proceeding when clear?
options: a:A flashing yellow light.,b:A solid green light.,c:A flashing red light.
note: A flashing red light means you must come to a complete stop, just as you would at a stop sign. After stopping, you must yield to any pedestrians and cross traffic, then proceed only when the way is clear and it is safe.

question: If an approaching vehicle is using high beams and fails to dim them, you should look toward:
options: a:Either side of the road.,b:The center of the road.,c:The right side of the road.
note: When another driver approaches with high beams and does not dim them, you should briefly glance toward the right edge of your lane or the right side of the road. This reduces glare, helps you avoid being blinded, and still lets you track your lane position using the right edge as a guide.

question: The most effective safety restraints in a crash are:
options: a:Only a lap and shoulder belt.,b:Only an airbag.,c:Both a lap/shoulder belt and an airbag.
note: The safest protection in a crash comes from using both the lap/shoulder belt and the airbag together. The seat belt keeps you properly positioned and prevents ejection, while the airbag provides additional cushioning in a collision. Never rely on an airbag alone without wearing your seat belt.

question: Why must you use extra caution around a pedestrian carrying a white cane?
options: a:They are police officers directing traffic.,b:They are deaf and cannot hear your horn.,c:They are likely blind and require yielding and extra caution.
note: A pedestrian with a white cane (or a guide dog) is usually blind or visually impaired. You must slow down, yield the right-of-way, and be prepared to stop. Give them extra space and time to cross safely, and never honk or rush them.

question: Regulatory traffic signs are usually which color?
options: a:Green,b:White (note: some regulatory signs, such as STOP and YIELD, are red and white),c:Blue
note: Most regulatory signs, such as speed limit, do not enter, and one-way signs, are white with black or red symbols and must be obeyed. However, not all regulatory signs are white: for example, STOP signs are red and white, and YIELD signs are red and white. The key idea is that regulatory signs state laws or rules you must follow.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parallel parking between two cars, what should you do first after signaling and checking traffic?
options: a:Turn your wheels to the right immediately.,b:Turn your wheels to the left immediately.,c:Pull up even with the car in front of the space
note: When parallel parking, after you signal and check traffic, you should first pull up so your vehicle is parallel and even with the car in front of the space. From that position you then begin turning the wheel and backing into the space. Starting your turn too early or late makes it harder to fit safely.

question: When dealing with pedestrians, what is the driver's obligation?
options: a:Only yield if the pedestrian is legally entitled to it.,b:Make sure the pedestrian is aware of the vehicle before yielding.,c:Yield the right-of-way to all pedestrians and do everything possible to avoid striking them.
note: Drivers must always use due care to avoid hitting pedestrians, even if the pedestrian is crossing illegally or unexpectedly. You should slow down, be prepared to stop, and yield the right‑of‑way to pedestrians to prevent injury, regardless of who technically has the right‑of‑way.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Drivers may not pass from either side of a ____ centerline.
options: a:Single broken yellow,b:Combination solid and broken yellow,c:Double solid yellow
note: A double solid yellow centerline means vehicles traveling in either direction may not cross the lines to pass. You must stay in your lane and only cross when making a permitted left turn into or from a driveway or side road, if allowed by local law.

question: You may pass another vehicle if the line dividing the lanes is what type of line?
options: a:Double solid yellow line.,b:Solid yellow line.,c:Broken white line.,d:Broken line on your side of a broken/solid yellow centerline.
note: You may pass another vehicle when the line closest to your lane is a broken line and it is safe to do so. Broken white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction and may be crossed to change lanes or pass. On two‑way roads, a broken yellow line on your side of a broken/solid combination also allows passing when safe.

question: When driving where children are playing, what should you expect?
options: a:They will always stop at the curb before crossing.,b:They will know when it's safe to cross.,c:They may run into the street without looking.
note: In areas where children are playing, you must assume they may act unpredictably, including running into the street without looking. Slow down, cover the brake, and be ready to stop quickly because children often misjudge vehicle speed and may not follow safety rules.

question: If someone is driving aggressively behind you, you should:
options: a:Speed up as they pass you.,b:Stare at the driver as they pass.,c:Attempt to get out of their way.
note: If someone is driving aggressively behind you, the safest response is to stay calm and create space. When it is safe, change lanes or otherwise move out of their way, avoid eye contact or gestures, and do not speed up or try to block them. Your goal is to reduce the risk of a confrontation or collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Unless posted otherwise, the speed limit in an urban residence district is:
options: a:40 miles per hour.,b:30 miles per hour.,c:55 miles per hour.
note: In many states, the default speed limit in an urban or residential district is 30 mph when no other limit is posted. Always watch for and obey posted signs, because local laws can set lower or higher limits in specific areas such as school zones or business districts.

question: On a highway marked by two solid yellow centerlines, you may:
options: a:Cross these lines only to make a left turn into or from a driveway, alley, or side road.,b:Never cross these lines under any circumstances.,c:Cross these lines to pass if no oncoming traffic is present.
note: Two solid yellow centerlines mean traffic in both directions must not cross the lines to pass. However, you may carefully cross double solid yellow lines to make a left turn into or from a driveway, alley, or side road when it is safe and legal to do so. You must never use them as a passing zone.

question: Which factors commonly cause traffic accidents?
options: a:Inattentive driving,b:Only vehicle defects.,c:Safe driving habits of other motorists.
note: Inattentive or distracted driving is one of the leading causes of crashes. Looking away from the road, using a phone, or letting your mind wander can cause you to miss hazards, react too slowly, or follow too closely. While vehicle defects can contribute to crashes, most collisions are caused by driver behavior, not by other motorists’ safe driving.

question: When are roads especially slippery due to rain?
options: a:During the first 10 to 15 minutes of a rainstorm.,b:The day after it rains.,c:Only after it has been raining for an hour.
note: When rain first begins, water mixes with oil, grease, and other residue on the road surface, making it especially slick during the first 10–15 minutes. As rain continues, much of this residue washes away and traction usually improves, though heavy rain can still reduce visibility and increase stopping distance.

question: What describes an inattentive driver?
options: a:Someone who only watches the vehicle directly ahead.,b:Someone who maintains eye contact while talking to a passenger.,c:Someone who daydreams or stares at objects off the roadway while driving.
note: An inattentive driver is not fully focused on the driving task. Daydreaming, staring at scenery or objects off the roadway, or mentally “zoning out” all reduce awareness of traffic, signals, and hazards and greatly increase crash risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a green arrow shown with a red light authorize you to do?
options: a:Turn only in the direction of the green arrow, if the intersection is clear.,b:Go straight ahead only.,c:Wait for a solid green circular light before moving in any direction.
note: A green arrow with a red circular light means you may proceed only in the direction of the arrow, and only after yielding to pedestrians and any traffic already in the intersection. All other movements remain stopped by the red light.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you come to an intersection with a flashing yellow light, you should:
options: a:Stop and wait for the light to change.,b:Make a U-turn because the intersection is closed.,c:Drive carefully through the intersection after yielding to any conflicting traffic.
note: A flashing yellow light means proceed with caution. Slow enough to check for cross traffic and pedestrians, yield to any conflicting traffic, and continue only when it is safe to do so. You do not have to stop if the way is clear.

question: It is important to slow down in which situations?
options: a:Whenever road, traffic, or visibility conditions make the posted speed unsafe.,b:On narrow or winding roads.,c:Only when the road is wet.
note: You must slow down whenever conditions make the normal speed unsafe, such as on narrow or winding roads, at intersections and railroad crossings, in heavy traffic, in poor visibility, or on wet, icy, or gravel surfaces. The posted speed limit is the maximum in ideal conditions, not a speed you must always maintain.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Unless otherwise posted, the maximum speed in a rural residence district is:
options: a:45 miles per hour.,b:25 miles per hour.,c:35 miles per hour.
note: Speed limits in residential and rural residential areas are set by each state and vary widely. Many states use 25 mph in residential areas, while others use 30 or 35 mph, and some distinguish between urban and rural residential districts. Because there is no single standard maximum speed for rural residence districts across the U.S., you must always follow the speed limit posted on local signs.

question: Who should wear seat belts for maximum effectiveness?
options: a:The driver only.,b:Only passengers on long trips.,c:All occupants of the vehicle.
note: Seat belts protect everyone in the vehicle, not just the driver. In a crash, unbelted passengers can be seriously injured and can also injure others by being thrown around inside the vehicle. For maximum safety, every occupant should wear a seat belt on every trip, no matter how short.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a posted speed limit indicate?
options: a:The exact safe speed you must always drive to avoid a ticket.,b:Only a recommended driving speed.,c:The maximum legal driving speed under ideal road and weather conditions.
note: A posted speed limit is the maximum legal speed allowed under ideal conditions, not a guaranteed safe speed in all situations. You must slow down when roads are wet, visibility is poor, traffic is heavy, or other conditions make the posted speed unsafe.

question: If a crossing guard directs traffic in a school zone, you must do what?
options: a:Copy surrounding traffic even if it contradicts the guard.,b:Follow the crossing guard's directions.,c:Assume they are not authorized to direct traffic.
note: Crossing guards are authorized to control traffic in school zones to protect children and pedestrians. You must obey their hand signals and instructions, even if they differ from traffic lights, and be ready to slow down, stop, and proceed only when they indicate it is safe.

question: What does a yellow-and-black diamond-shaped sign indicate?
options: a:Traffic laws and regulations you must obey.,b:A warning about conditions on or near the road ahead.,c:Directions to nearby cities and towns.
note: Yellow-and-black diamond-shaped signs are warning signs. They alert you to upcoming road conditions or hazards such as curves, intersections, pedestrian crossings, or changes in road surface so you can slow down and drive with extra caution.

question: When approaching a railroad crossing with warning signs, what should you be prepared to do?
options: a:Proceed without slowing unless you see a train.,b:Cross quickly if a train is approaching.,c:Slow down, look, listen, and be prepared to stop.
note: When you see warning signs for a railroad crossing, you must slow down, look and listen for trains, and be prepared to stop. Never try to beat a train across the tracks. If lights are flashing, gates are down, or a train is clearly approaching, you must stop at the proper distance and wait until it is completely safe to cross.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How close to a bridge, viaduct, or tunnel is passing prohibited?
options: a:Within 100 feet.,b:Within 300 feet.,c:Within 200 feet.
note: You must not begin or be in a passing maneuver within 100 feet of a bridge, viaduct, or tunnel because your view and others’ view may be restricted. Limited sight distance makes it harder to see oncoming traffic or hazards, so the law prohibits passing in these areas to prevent head‑on collisions.

question: For persons age 21 and older, it is illegal to drive with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of at least:
options: a:0.02 percent,b:0.08 percent,c:0.05 percent
note: For drivers age 21 and older in the U.S., it is illegal to drive with a BAC of 0.08% or higher. At or above 0.08%, you are considered legally impaired, and you can be arrested and convicted of DUI even if you feel capable of driving.

question: A red and white triangular sign at an intersection means you must:
options: a:Speed up if an emergency vehicle is approaching.,b:Always come to a full stop.,c:Yield — slow and be prepared to stop if necessary.
note: A red and white triangle is a yield sign. You must slow down, be ready to stop, and yield the right‑of‑way to traffic and pedestrians already in or close to the intersection. You only stop if needed to let others go first.

question: How can stress affect your driving?
options: a:By decreasing your chance of an accident.,b:By causing you to fall asleep at the wheel.,c:By reducing your ability to focus and concentrate on driving.
note: Stress and strong emotions can distract you, narrow your attention, and slow your reaction time. This reduces your ability to notice hazards, make good decisions, and control the vehicle smoothly, increasing your crash risk.

question: When approaching an accident scene you should:
options: a:Always stop and watch.,b:Drive toward the scene to see what happened.,c:Stop only if you are involved or emergency help has not yet arrived.
note: When approaching a crash, keep moving safely unless you are involved or emergency help has not arrived and you can safely assist. Unnecessary stopping creates additional hazards, blocks traffic, and can cause more collisions.

question: When is it legal to stop or park along the shoulder of a freeway?
options: a:If no part of your vehicle is on the roadway.,b:Only in an emergency.,c:As long as you turn on your four-way flashers.
note: On freeways, stopping or parking on the shoulder is only allowed for emergencies such as breakdowns or medical issues. If you must stop, pull as far onto the shoulder as possible and turn on your hazard lights so other drivers can see you.

question: A diamond-shaped traffic sign is normally used to:
options: a:Indicate a school crossing.,b:Indicate an interstate route.,c:Warn of a road hazard or special condition.
note: Diamond-shaped signs are warning signs. They alert drivers to hazards or special conditions ahead, such as curves, merging traffic, or pedestrian crossings, so you can slow down and be prepared.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Who must yield when a driver is turning and a pedestrian is crossing without a traffic light?
options: a:Whoever is slower.,b:Whoever started moving last.,c:The driver must yield to the pedestrian.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians who are crossing the street at intersections, even if there is no traffic light or painted crosswalk. Pedestrians in or entering the driver’s path at an intersection have the right-of-way.

question: What is likely to happen when alcohol is combined with another drug?
options: a:The effects of both may be reduced.,b:Nothing will happen.,c:The effects of both the alcohol and the drug may be increased.
note: Combining alcohol with other drugs, including many prescription or over-the-counter medicines, can greatly increase the effects of both. This can severely reduce judgment, coordination, and reaction time, making driving extremely dangerous.

question: Which statement about winter driving is NOT true?
options: a:Using cruise control in winter weather is safe.,b:Checking antifreeze and washer fluid is especially important in winter.,c:Winter is the most difficult driving season.
note: In winter, roads can be icy or snowy and traction is reduced, so it is one of the most difficult driving seasons. You should not use cruise control on slippery roads because you need full control of your speed. It is also especially important to check antifreeze and washer fluid so your vehicle can operate safely in cold conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto an interstate from an entrance ramp, you should:
options: a:Have the right-of-way over traffic on the interstate.,b:Force your way into traffic if necessary.,c:Yield to drivers already on the interstate.
note: When entering an interstate, you must yield to traffic already on the highway. Use the entrance ramp and acceleration lane to reach the speed of traffic, signal, and merge only when there is a safe gap. Do not assume other drivers will move or slow down for you.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing on a multilane highway you should:
options: a:Watch for oncoming traffic in the opposite direction.,b:Always pass only on the right.,c:Be sure the passing lane is clear before changing lanes.
note: On a multilane highway, always make sure the lane you want to move into is clear before changing lanes to pass. Check mirrors, look over your shoulder for blind spots, signal, and then move over when it is safe. Passing is usually done on the left unless specific conditions allow a safe pass on the right.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to turn left, what should drivers do?
options: a:Signal only if other traffic is present.,b:Slow down gradually without checking mirrors.,c:Watch for oncoming vehicles and pedestrians and yield when necessary.
note: Before turning left, signal well in advance, check your mirrors and blind spots, and move into the proper lane. You must yield to oncoming traffic going straight or turning right and to pedestrians in the crosswalk. Begin your turn only when the path is clear and it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you encounter a flashing red light at an intersection, what must you do?
options: a:Slow down and drive carefully through.,b:Wait for a flashing green light.,c:Come to a complete stop and proceed only when the way is clear.
note: A flashing red light means you must come to a complete stop, just as you would at a stop sign. Stop before the crosswalk or stop line, yield to pedestrians and any cross traffic, and proceed only when the intersection is clear and it is safe to go.

question: If your vehicle's accelerator sticks while driving, which action should you take?
options: a:Slam on the brakes immediately and hold them.,b:Turn on your hazard flashers,c:Blow your horn continuously until help arrives.
note: If your accelerator sticks, keep control of the vehicle: shift to neutral, apply steady brake pressure, and steer to the side of the road and out of traffic. Once you are safely off the roadway, turn off the engine to stop the engine power, being careful not to turn the key to the lock position so you do not lose steering control. Use hazard flashers to warn other drivers while you slow and pull over.

question: When sharing the road with a large truck remember trucks generally:
options: a:Require longer distances to stop than smaller vehicles.,b:Require less time to pass on a downgrade.,c:Require a smaller turning radius than smaller vehicles.
note: Large trucks are much heavier than passenger cars, so they need more distance and time to stop, especially at higher speeds or when loaded. You should avoid cutting in front of a truck or braking suddenly because the truck may not be able to stop in time.

question: If your car breaks down on the highway, you should:
options: a:Use your four-way flashers,b:Sound your horn to attract passing motorists' attention.,c:Sit in your car and wait for help without signaling
note: If your car breaks down on a highway, signal and carefully move as far off the roadway as possible, then turn on your four-way flashers so other drivers can see that your vehicle is disabled. This helps prevent collisions and alerts others to use extra caution when passing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a stop sign with no stop line or crosswalk, you may proceed only:
options: a:After slowing down to check for cross traffic.,b:After stopping at least 20 feet before the intersection.,c:After coming to a complete stop and verifying it is safe to proceed.
note: At a stop sign with no marked stop line or crosswalk, you must come to a complete stop before entering the intersection, then look for traffic and pedestrians in all directions. Proceed only when you are sure it is safe and you will not interfere with other road users.

question: What colors are used on highway destination/distance signs (like exit signs)?
options: a:Black background with white letters.,b:Yellow background with black letters.,c:Green background with white letters or symbols.
note: In the United States, highway guide signs that show destinations, directions, and distances use a green background with white letters or symbols. These signs help drivers navigate to cities, exits, and points of interest along the route.

question: Why is night driving often harder than daytime driving?
options: a:Because visibility is reduced in the dark.,b:Because it is more likely to rain at night.,c:Because cars overheat more easily at night.
note: Night driving is harder because you can see less of the road and its surroundings. Headlights only illuminate a limited distance, making it harder to spot hazards in time. You should reduce your speed, use proper headlights, and make sure you can stop within the distance you can see ahead.

question: When a funeral procession is present, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:Any other driver.,b:A pedestrian.,c:The funeral procession.
note: Drivers, pedestrians, and bicyclists must yield the right-of-way to a properly identified funeral procession. The vehicles in the procession travel together and generally proceed through intersections as a unit when allowed, so other road users must wait until the procession has passed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is driving below the posted speed limit illegal?
options: a:Only while driving in rural areas.,b:When in heavy traffic in a construction zone.,c:When driving so slowly that you disrupt the normal flow of traffic.
note: Driving significantly below the normal speed of traffic can be illegal if it interferes with the safe and reasonable flow of vehicles. If you are moving so slowly that you block or disrupt traffic without a good reason (such as bad weather or heavy congestion), you may be required to pull over and let faster traffic pass.

question: What road markings or signals direct drivers into proper turning lanes on some highways?
options: a:Flashing red lights.,b:Arrows painted or displayed to indicate lane purposes.,c:White lines on the side of the road only.
note: Arrows painted on the pavement or shown on overhead lane-use signals tell you which lanes are for turning and which are for going straight. Following these arrows helps keep traffic organized and prevents last‑second lane changes at intersections.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A posted speed limit represents what?
options: a:The maximum legal speed under ideal conditions (and sometimes a posted minimum where indicated).,b:The legal speed under dangerous conditions.,c:A suggested safe speed for the area.
note: A posted speed limit is the maximum legal speed allowed under ideal conditions, and in some areas there may also be a posted minimum speed. You must always adjust your speed to road, traffic, and weather conditions, and drive slower than the limit whenever conditions are not ideal.

question: What should a driver do if going much slower than the speed limit and causing a backup?
options: a:Pull off the road and allow vehicles to pass.,b:Refuse to let following cars pass.,c:Continue; slower speeds are always safer.
note: If you are traveling much slower than the speed limit and causing a line of vehicles to back up, you should safely pull off the road where possible and let them pass. Very slow driving can be just as hazardous as speeding because it disrupts traffic flow and may lead to unsafe passing.

question: On slippery roads you should do which of the following?
options: a:Drive as you would on dry roads.,b:Increase your following distance.,c:Use alternate routes only.
note: On slippery roads your tires have less traction, so it takes longer to stop and easier to skid. You should slow down and increase your following distance so you have more time and space to brake gently and avoid sudden steering or braking.

question: If you notice other drivers behaving angrily on the road, you should:
options: a:Make eye contact to let them know you won't be intimidated.,b:React with hand gestures to show your displeasure.,c:Distance yourself from the situation (physically and mentally).
note: When other drivers are angry or aggressive, avoid eye contact, do not respond with gestures, and do not engage. Safest practice is to distance yourself physically by changing lanes or letting them go ahead, and mentally by staying calm and focused on your own driving.

question: If you are in another driver's blind spot, what should you do?
options: a:Stay there until you need to pass.,b:Keep a steady pace in the blind spot.,c:Move forward or fall back so the driver can see you.
note: Blind spots are areas a driver cannot see in their mirrors. If you are in another driver’s blind spot, they may change lanes or turn into you without seeing you. Either move ahead so you are clearly visible in their mirrors or drop back so you are well behind their vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before making a left turn you must:
options: a:Swing to the right side of your lane before turning.,b:Sound your horn to warn others.,c:Yield to oncoming vehicles and pedestrians.
note: Before making a left turn, you must yield the right-of-way to oncoming vehicles and to pedestrians in the crosswalk. Do not turn if it would force oncoming traffic to slow or stop, and complete the turn only when it is safe and legal to do so.

question: If you become stranded during a snowstorm, what should you do?
options: a:Lie down inside the car and go to sleep.,b:Wait in your vehicle for help to arrive.,c:Leave the car and walk for assistance.
note: If you are stranded in a snowstorm, it is usually safest to stay with your vehicle. Your car provides shelter and is easier for rescuers to find than a person on foot. Run the engine only occasionally for heat, with a window slightly open and the exhaust pipe clear of snow to prevent carbon monoxide buildup.

question: What is the safest way to drive through a curve?
options: a:Slow down as you enter the curve and accelerate gradually as you exit.,b:Keep a constant speed throughout the curve.,c:Speed up as you enter the curve and slow down as you exit.
note: Slow down before and as you enter a curve so your tires can grip the road and you can steer smoothly. As you come out of the curve and your vehicle begins to straighten, you can gradually accelerate. Entering too fast or accelerating into the curve can cause you to lose control, especially on wet or slippery roads.

question: Where should you keep a space cushion around your vehicle?
options: a:Only in front of your vehicle.,b:Only on the left and right sides.,c:On all sides — front, rear, and sides.
note: A space cushion is the open space around your vehicle that gives you time to see and react to hazards. You should keep safe space in front, behind, and on both sides whenever possible. This extra room lets you brake, change lanes, or steer away from danger without sudden, unsafe movements.

question: When approached by an emergency vehicle using lights or siren, you must:
options: a:Pull to the right and turn on your four-way flashers.,b:Pull to the right and slow down.,c:Pull to the right side of the road and stop immediately.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches using lights or siren, you must yield the right-of-way by pulling as far to the right side of the road as safely possible and stopping. Stay stopped until the emergency vehicle has passed. This creates a clear path so they can respond quickly and safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: In a vertically arranged traffic signal, what is the correct top-to-bottom order of the lights?
options: a:Red,b:Yellow,c:Green
note: On a standard vertical traffic signal, the red light is always at the top, yellow is in the middle, and green is at the bottom. Knowing this order helps you understand the signal even if the colors are hard to see due to glare, weather, or color-vision issues.

question: When parking uphill on a street with a curb, which way should you turn your front wheels?
options: a:Keep the wheels straight and set the parking brake.,b:Turn the front wheels away from the curb.,c:Turn the front wheels toward the curb.
note: When parking uphill with a curb, turn your front wheels away from the curb and set the parking brake. If the brakes fail, the vehicle will roll back slightly and the front tire will rest against the curb, helping prevent the car from rolling into traffic.

question: Which factors affect braking distance?
options: a:Speed,b:Only the vehicle's weight.,c:Only the driver’s reaction time.
note: Braking distance is the distance your vehicle travels from the time you apply the brakes until the vehicle stops. It increases sharply with speed and is also affected by brake condition, tire condition, road surface, and weather. Reaction time affects total stopping distance, but not the braking distance itself.

question: What driving habit helps conserve gasoline?
options: a:Accelerating quickly from stops.,b:Sitting in the driveway with the engine running.,c:Slowing down gradually and avoiding unnecessary braking.
note: Smooth, gradual driving—looking ahead, slowing down early, and avoiding unnecessary braking and rapid acceleration—reduces fuel use. Hard starts, idling, and sudden stops waste gasoline.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When an emergency vehicle uses sirens or flashing lights, what must drivers do?
options: a:Stop immediately in your lane and wait for it to pass no matter where you are.,b:Ignore it if you are in a hurry.,c:Yield the right-of-way by pulling to the right and stopping, and follow any instructions it gives.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches using sirens or flashing lights, you must immediately yield the right‑of‑way by pulling over to the right side of the road and stopping, when safe, and then remain stopped until it has passed. Always follow any directions given by emergency personnel and be alert for additional emergency vehicles following.

question: On slippery roads you should:
options: a:Drive the speed limit with no extra caution.,b:Drive more quickly.,c:Slow down.
note: On slippery roads, reduce your speed and make all movements gently. Drive slower than the posted speed limit if conditions are poor, and avoid sudden braking, acceleration, or sharp steering that could cause a skid.

question: When children ride in a vehicle, they should:
options: a:Stand on the floor in the back of the vehicle.,b:Be properly fastened in an appropriate child safety seat if too small for a regular belt.,c:Be safely held by a strong adult.
note: Children who are too small for a regular seat belt must be secured in an appropriate child safety seat or booster seat that is correctly installed. Holding a child in your arms or allowing them to stand is extremely dangerous in a crash.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must you signal while turning or changing lanes?
options: a:Only when driving at night.,b:Always,c:Only when other vehicles are present.
note: You must always signal before turning, changing lanes, or pulling away from a curb, regardless of time of day or whether you see other vehicles. Signaling lets other road users anticipate your actions and helps prevent collisions.

question: What effect does alcohol have on driving skills and judgment?
options: a:It has no effect on either.,b:It helps driving skills but harms judgment.,c:It harms both driving skills and judgment.
note: Alcohol slows reaction time, reduces coordination, and affects vision, while also weakening judgment and self-control. This combination makes it harder to drive safely and more likely that you will take dangerous risks.

question: A pentagonal (five-sided) traffic sign warns drivers they are near:
options: a:A no passing zone.,b:A speed limit change.,c:A school zone or school crossing.
note: A five-sided (pentagon) sign is used for school zones and school crossings. When you see this shape, watch carefully for children and be prepared to slow down or stop as required by posted signs.

question: What does a solid red arrow in a traffic signal mean?
options: a:It has the same meaning as a circular red light; you must stop.,b:It is never used.,c:It means drivers may turn in the arrow direction.
note: A solid red arrow means you must stop and remain stopped if you are intending to move in the direction of the arrow. You may not turn in that direction while the red arrow is displayed; wait for a green arrow or green light allowing the movement.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the correct procedure when using a freeway exit ramp?
options: a:Slow down before you move onto the exit ramp.,b:Maintain your freeway speed until the ramp ends.,c:Slow down once you are on the exit ramp.
note: On a freeway, stay at traffic speed until you enter the exit ramp’s deceleration lane. Once you are on the ramp, then reduce speed to match the posted ramp speed or conditions. Slowing on the main freeway can cause rear-end collisions.

question: To avoid being in a truck or bus driver's blind spot you should:
options: a:Flash your lights at them.,b:Never pass them.,c:Avoid driving alongside them and avoid tailgating.
note: Large trucks and buses have big blind spots along both sides and directly behind the vehicle. To stay visible and safe, avoid driving right alongside them for long periods and never follow too closely. Instead, pass promptly and leave extra space so the driver can see you in their mirrors.

question: A solid yellow arrow traffic signal means:
options: a:It is not used as a traffic control signal.,b:Drivers may turn in the direction indicated without caution.,c:The same as a circular yellow light — prepare to stop.
note: A solid yellow arrow means the protected turn phase is ending. It has the same meaning as a circular yellow light for that movement: the signal is about to turn red. You should slow down and prepare to stop if you can do so safely; only complete the turn if you are already in the intersection and cannot stop safely.

question: A road work area or work zone may be which of the following?
options: a:Moving or stationary.,b:A place where drivers do not have to slow down or pay attention.,c:Marked with black and white signs.
note: Work zones can be stationary, like a fixed construction site, or moving, such as a line-painting or maintenance vehicle traveling along the road. They are usually marked with orange signs, cones, or arrow boards, and drivers must slow down, obey posted work zone speeds, and pay extra attention to workers and equipment.

question: How does increasing your vehicle's speed affect your field of vision?
options: a:It increases your field of vision.,b:It decreases your field of vision.,c:It makes it easier to see cross traffic.
note: As your speed increases, your field of vision narrows. You see less to the sides and tend to focus more on what is directly ahead. This makes it easier to miss pedestrians, cyclists, or cross traffic, so higher speeds require extra caution and scanning.

question: Which types of drugs can impair driving ability?
options: a:Only illegal drugs.,b:Prescription and over-the-counter medications,c:Only alcohol-related medicines.
note: Many substances can impair driving, including illegal drugs, prescription medications, and over‑the‑counter medicines. Some can make you drowsy, slow your reactions, or affect judgment and coordination. Always read labels and follow medical advice; driving under the influence of any impairing drug is dangerous and can be illegal.

question: Foggy conditions require which of these actions?
options: a:Turn on your low-beam headlights.,b:Turn on your hazard lights only.,c:Drive at the posted maximum speed.
note: In fog, always use low‑beam headlights. High beams reflect off the water droplets in the fog and shine back at you, making it harder to see. Slow down and use low beams so you can see the road and be seen by others.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A red flashing traffic light is equivalent to which traffic control device?
options: a:A stop sign.,b:A steady red light only.,c:A yield sign.
note: A flashing red light means you must come to a complete stop, just as you would at a stop sign. After stopping, yield to traffic and pedestrians, then proceed only when it is safe.

question: What does a “No standing” sign mean at a location?
options: a:You may stop only briefly to pick up or discharge passengers.,b:You may park there if you stay with the vehicle.,c:You may never stop there for any reason.
note: A “No standing” sign means you may stop only long enough to pick up or drop off passengers. You may not wait there, load or unload goods, or park the vehicle.

question: What should you do before switching on the ignition?
options: a:Confirm only adult passengers are belted.,b:Only make sure children are belted.,c:Buckle your seat belt and ensure passengers are buckled.
note: Before starting the vehicle, buckle your own seat belt and make sure every passenger is properly buckled. Making this a habit greatly reduces the risk of injury in a crash.

question: If you face an oncoming car on your left and a bicyclist on your right, what should you do?
options: a:Pull onto the shoulder to pass between both.,b:Split the difference and move between them.,c:Let the oncoming car pass first
note: When you have an oncoming car on the left and a bicyclist on the right, let the oncoming car pass first. This gives you more space to move left and pass the bicyclist safely without squeezing between the two hazards.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it appropriate to sound your horn?
options: a:Whenever you have to stop quickly.,b:When passing another car.,c:If you have lost control of your vehicle and need to alert others.
note: Use your horn to warn other road users of immediate danger, such as when you lose control of your vehicle or when another driver may not see you. Do not use the horn just because you are stopping quickly or to signal routine passing; unnecessary horn use can startle others and is often illegal.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are required to stop your vehicle:
options: a:Only when a police officer orders you to.,b:At an intersection with a stop sign.,c:Only where there is a flashing yellow light.
note: You must come to a complete stop at stop signs, at steady red traffic lights (unless a specific sign or signal allows otherwise), and whenever directed by a police officer or traffic control person. Stopping is not limited to police orders; it is required at all controlled intersections where a stop is indicated.

question: When must you stop for a school bus on a two-lane highway?
options: a:Only when the bus is facing you and its lights are flashing.,b:Only if the bus is parked on the shoulder with no one aboard.,c:When the bus is stopped and its red lights are flashing.
note: On a two-lane road with no physical divider, traffic in both directions must stop when a school bus is stopped with its red lights flashing and stop arm extended. Remain stopped until the lights stop flashing and the bus moves or the driver signals you to proceed.

question: Highway pavement markings generally:
options: a:Provide information and guidance for drivers.,b:Are usually not important.,c:Are only found in construction zones.
note: Pavement markings guide drivers by showing lane positions, turn lanes, crosswalks, and passing zones, and by warning of upcoming conditions such as lane reductions. They are an essential part of the traffic control system and must be obeyed just like signs and signals.

question: To make night driving safer you should:
options: a:Increase your following distance to give more stopping time.,b:Always use your high beams.,c:Drive at the same following distance as daytime
note: At night, your visibility and ability to judge distance are reduced, so you should increase your following distance to give yourself more time to react and stop. Use high beams only when appropriate and dim them for oncoming traffic or when following another vehicle closely.

question: How do blind spots of larger vehicles compare to those of smaller cars?
options: a:Larger vehicles have smaller blind spots.,b:Larger vehicles have larger blind spots.,c:Larger vehicles have no blind spots.
note: Larger vehicles like trucks, buses, and SUVs sit higher and have longer bodies, which creates bigger areas around them that the driver cannot see in mirrors. These larger blind spots are along the sides, directly behind, and sometimes directly in front of the vehicle. You should avoid driving for long periods in these areas because the driver may not know you are there.

question: If you are worried, nervous, angry, or crying before driving you should:
options: a:Drive faster because you are more alert.,b:Drive no differently than usual.,c:Take time to calm down and focus on driving before starting the engine.
note: Strong emotions such as anger, worry, or crying can distract you, slow your reactions, and cause poor decisions in traffic. Before driving, take time to calm down and regain focus so your full attention is on the road and other road users.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you not cross a single broken white or yellow line?
options: a:When the car in front is disabled.,b:When turning left into a driveway.,c:When doing so would interfere with traffic.
note: A single broken white or yellow line means you may cross it to change lanes or pass, but only when it is safe and legal. You must not cross if doing so would interfere with other traffic, such as forcing another driver to brake or swerve. Always check for enough space and clear visibility before crossing.

question: Two solid white lines across a lane indicate a crosswalk. What must drivers do when pedestrians are in a crosswalk?
options: a:Proceed because no one has right-of-way there.,b:Give pedestrians the right-of-way and stop for them.,c:Assert that motor vehicles have the right-of-way.
note: Crosswalks mark where pedestrians may cross the road. When a pedestrian is in a marked or unmarked crosswalk on your side of the road, or close enough to be in danger, you must yield the right-of-way and stop if necessary. Never drive through a crosswalk while pedestrians are crossing.

question: If you drink alcohol socially, which action helps ensure safe driving?
options: a:Drink coffee before driving.,b:Take a cold shower before driving.,c:Ride home with a friend who has not been drinking.
note: Once alcohol is in your system, only time can reduce your blood alcohol concentration. Coffee, cold showers, or exercise do not make you sober enough to drive. The safest choice after drinking is to not drive at all and instead ride with a sober driver, use a taxi, or use a rideshare service.

question: What is the primary purpose of regulatory signs?
options: a:To indicate what drivers must or must not do.,b:To be diamond-shaped and yellow or green.,c:To mark every location with present danger.
note: Regulatory signs tell you what you must do or must not do under the law, such as speed limits, no parking, or one-way directions. They are about legal requirements, not just warnings or general information.

question: What should car drivers remember about large trucks?
options: a:They can stop more quickly than cars.,b:They have large blind spots and need more room to maneuver and stop.,c:They need less room to turn than passenger vehicles.
note: Large trucks have big blind spots on all sides and are heavier, so they need more distance to stop and more room to turn and maneuver. You should give them extra space and avoid lingering in their blind spots.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a stop sign you should stop and then look in which order?
options: a:Check left, then right, then left again.,b:Check straight ahead only.,c:Right
note: At a stop sign, come to a complete stop, then look left, right, and left again before moving. Traffic that can hit you first usually comes from the left, so you check that direction carefully, then the right, then left again to confirm it is still clear.

question: When stopped on an uphill slope, when should you allow a larger space cushion?
options: a:At a stop sign only.,b:When stopped on an incline.,c:When stopped at an intersection only.
note: When you are stopped on an uphill slope, leave extra space between you and the vehicle ahead. When traffic starts moving, the vehicle in front may roll backward slightly before moving forward, and the extra space helps prevent a collision.

question: A bicyclist who disobeys traffic laws:
options: a:Will always receive a warning from law enforcement.,b:Can be ticketed.,c:Is in the right because bicyclists don’t have to obey traffic laws.
note: Bicyclists generally must follow the same traffic laws as drivers, including stopping at stop signs and obeying signals. If they break these laws, they can receive tickets just like motor vehicle drivers.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When a stop is required at an intersection but there are no stop lines or crosswalk markings, you should:
options: a:You are still required to come to a complete stop.,b:Stop only at a point where you can see 200 feet in both directions.,c:Come to a complete stop at the point nearest the intersecting roadway where you have a clear view of oncoming traffic.
note: When there is a stop sign but no stop line or crosswalk, you must still come to a complete stop. Stop at the point just before entering the intersecting roadway where you have a clear view of traffic on the cross street, then proceed when it is safe.

question: When preparing to change lanes, which action is crucial?
options: a:Signal your intentions ahead of the lane change.,b:Make sure the lane is clear before entering.,c:Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder.
note: Before changing lanes you must: signal, check your mirrors, check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder, and then move only when the lane is clear. Checking the blind spot is essential, but the critical safety requirement is that you do not enter the lane until you know it is clear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If an officer is directing traffic at an intersection, you should:
options: a:Honk at the officer to get their attention.,b:Follow the directions given by the officer.,c:Follow the traffic signal instead of the officer.
note: If a police officer or other authorized person is directing traffic, you must follow their hand signals and instructions, even if traffic lights or signs say something different. Their directions temporarily override normal signals and signs to keep traffic safe and orderly.

question: An arrow painted on the pavement indicates that drivers in that lane:
options: a:Must make the movement indicated by the arrow.,b:Must always stop before making the movement.,c:May make the movement if they choose.
note: Lane-use arrows painted on the pavement show what movement is required from that lane, such as straight, left turn, or right turn. When you are in a lane with a single arrow, you must make the movement shown, unless a sign or signal specifically allows something different.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a highway you should signal before a turn at least:
options: a:500 feet.,b:100 feet.,c:300 feet.
note: On higher-speed roads and highways, you should signal well in advance so other drivers have time to react. Many states require at least 500 feet before turning on a highway, while 100 feet is common for lower-speed roads. Signaling early improves safety and predictability.

question: As alcohol accumulates in your bloodstream it typically:
options: a:Causes alcohol to metabolize more quickly.,b:Makes you feel less confident.,c:Slows down your reactions.
note: Alcohol in the bloodstream slows your brain and nervous system. As your blood alcohol concentration rises, your reaction time gets slower, your judgment gets worse, and you are more likely to make driving errors. Alcohol does not speed up its own metabolism, and many people actually feel more confident even though their driving skills are getting worse.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When a traffic signal turns green, you should:
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to pedestrians and traffic already in the intersection.,b:Back up slowly if the way is blocked.,c:Accelerate as quickly as possible to clear the intersection.
note: A green light means you may go only after you first yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk and any vehicles already in the intersection. You must not back up into traffic or accelerate aggressively; instead, proceed when the intersection is clear and it is safe.

question: How should you safely pass a bicycle?
options: a:Slow down and give as much space as possible when passing.,b:Honk to alert them and pass quickly.,c:Drive in the bicycle lane until you can pass the rider.
note: When passing a bicyclist, slow down and give them as much space as you safely can, following any state minimum (often at least 3 feet). Avoid honking in a way that could startle them, and never drive in a bicycle lane except where specifically allowed for turning or when safely merging across it.

question: Which of the following can impair a person's driving ability?
options: a:Alcohol.,b:Any medication.,c:A lack of sleep.
note: Driving can be impaired by alcohol, many medications (including some that are legal and prescribed), illegal drugs, and drowsiness. A lack of sleep clearly impairs driving ability, and medications can as well, but not every medication does. Alcohol is always impairing, but it is not the only cause. The safest answer here is the one that correctly identifies a condition that always impairs driving: being sleep-deprived.

question: What causes 'highway hypnosis'?
options: a:Too much sleep the night before your trip.,b:Staring straight ahead at the roadway for long periods of time.,c:Frequent rest stops
note: Highway hypnosis is a trance-like state that can occur when you stare straight ahead at the road for long periods without actively scanning. Your mind drifts, and you may not fully register what is happening around you. To prevent this, move your eyes regularly, check mirrors, take breaks, and stay mentally engaged with the driving task.

question: What is the correct method to check your blind spots?
options: a:Look only in your side mirrors.,b:Turn your head and look over your shoulder.,c:Check only the rearview mirror.
note: Blind spots are areas you cannot see with your mirrors alone. To check them, you must briefly turn your head and look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move, in addition to using your mirrors.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two vehicles enter an intersection from different highways at the same time, which vehicle must yield?
options: a:Either vehicle may proceed first.,b:The vehicle on the right must yield to the vehicle on the left.,c:The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection where two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. This right‑of‑way rule helps prevent confusion and collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before changing lanes on a multilane highway you should do what?
options: a:Check rearview and side mirrors and glance over your shoulder.,b:Sound your horn.,c:Turn on your headlights.
note: Before changing lanes, check your rearview and side mirrors, then quickly glance over your shoulder to check your blind spot in the direction of the lane change. Only move when the lane is clear and it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a green arrow on a traffic signal mean for the lane it controls?
options: a:A green arrow is used only on one-way streets.,b:Traffic in that lane may turn in the arrow's direction; it has the same general meaning as a circular green but requires turning.,c:You may proceed only if a circular green light is also lit.
note: A green arrow means you have a protected movement in the direction of the arrow. Traffic in that lane may proceed only in the arrow’s direction and must turn as indicated, yielding to pedestrians and any vehicles already in the intersection.

question: If you see an animal on the roadway, what is the recommended action?
options: a:Pass as closely as possible to minimize delay.,b:Honk repeatedly to move it quickly.,c:Pass the animal slowly and cautiously to avoid startling it.
note: When you see an animal on or near the road, slow down and pass it cautiously, leaving as much space as possible. Sudden movements, speeding, or loud honking can startle the animal and increase the risk of a collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a driver's left arm and hand are extended upward, what is the driver's intended action?
options: a:The driver intends to turn left.,b:The driver intends to turn right.,c:The driver intends to stop.
note: When a driver’s left arm is extended straight out, it means a left turn. When the left arm is extended upward at the elbow, it signals a right turn. When the left arm is extended downward, it signals slowing or stopping.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your interstate exit, what should you do?
options: a:Make a U-turn to return to the exit.,b:Continue to the next exit and do not attempt a dangerous turnback.,c:Quickly cut across traffic to make the exit.
note: If you miss your exit on an interstate, stay calm, keep going, and take the next exit. Never stop, back up, or cut across lanes at the last second, because those maneuvers can cause serious crashes at highway speeds.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Unless otherwise posted, what is the speed limit in a posted school zone in New Hampshire?
options: a:20 miles per hour.,b:10 miles per hour below the usual posted limit.,c:15 miles per hour.
note: In New Hampshire, the speed limit in any posted school zone is exactly 10 miles per hour below the usual posted speed limit. This is active from 45 minutes before school opening until opening, and from closing until 45 minutes after closing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your exit on a freeway you should:
options: a:Stop and back up to the exit.,b:Make the turn quickly from your current lane of travel.,c:Continue to the next exit or suitable turnaround and do not back up.
note: If you miss your exit on a freeway, continue to the next exit or another safe place to turn around. Never stop, back up, or make a sudden turn from the wrong lane, because traffic is moving fast and drivers behind you will not expect it.

question: On a two-lane road without a bicycle lane, what is the safest method to pass a bicyclist?
options: a:Drive in the oncoming lane only when it is safe and legal, leaving plenty of space as you pass.,b:Force the bicyclist to move by honking.,c:Slow down and pass only when you can give the bicyclist plenty of space, at least 3 feet where required.
note: On a two-lane road without a bicycle lane, slow down and pass the bicyclist only when it is safe, leaving plenty of space—at least 3 feet where required or recommended by law. Do not drive in a bike lane, crowd the bicyclist, or use your horn to force them over, as this can startle them and cause a crash.

question: Why should you be cautious when passing a bicycle?
options: a:Because bicycles travel much faster than cars.,b:The bicycle always has the right-of-way.,c:Oncoming traffic may not see you and the bicyclist may swerve to avoid hazards.
note: When passing a bicyclist, you must allow extra space because bicycles are small, can be hard for others to see, and may need to swerve suddenly to avoid potholes, debris, or opening car doors. You also need to be sure oncoming traffic can see you and that you have enough room to pass safely without crowding the bicyclist.

question: When is hand-over-hand steering recommended?
options: a:For normal cruising activity on highways.,b:When anti-lock brakes are engaged.,c:When making low-speed turns such as at intersections or parking.
note: Hand-over-hand steering is used mainly for low-speed, tight turns such as at intersections, driveways, and parking maneuvers. This method lets you turn the wheel quickly and maintain good control when making sharper turns at slower speeds.

question: You should look over your shoulder to check your blind spot when you are:
options: a:Turning left or right.,b:Pulling toward or away from a curb.,c:Changing lanes.
note: You must look over your shoulder to check your blind spot whenever you move laterally into an area your mirrors cannot show, such as when changing lanes or pulling toward or away from a curb. A quick glance over the appropriate shoulder helps you see vehicles, bicycles, or pedestrians that may be hidden in your blind spot.

question: If an emergency vehicle with flashing red or blue lights is approaching, what should you do?
options: a:Continue driving but try to stay out of its way.,b:Pull to the side of the road and stop completely when safe to do so.,c:See if you can reach your destination before it catches up.
note: When an emergency vehicle with flashing red or blue lights and a siren approaches, you must yield the right-of-way. Safely pull to the right side of the road and stop until it has passed. If you are in an intersection, clear the intersection first, then pull over as soon as it is safe.

question: Turning your head to check a blind spot before changing lanes is:
options: a:A bad driving habit.,b:A good driving habit.,c:Unnecessary.
note: Turning your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes is a key part of safe driving. Mirrors do not show everything around your vehicle, so a quick glance over your shoulder helps you spot vehicles, motorcycles, or bicycles that might be in the blind spot.

question: When you see or hear an emergency vehicle, what is the correct action?
options: a:Stop immediately where you are.,b:Proceed slowly and let it pass.,c:Drive as far right as safely possible and stop.
note: On most roads, when an emergency vehicle approaches using lights or siren, you must pull as far to the right side of the road as is safe and come to a stop. This creates a clear path for the emergency vehicle and reduces the chance of a collision. Do not stop suddenly in the lane or continue driving alongside the emergency vehicle.

question: Which factor does NOT affect stopping distance?
options: a:Your reaction time.,b:The time of day.,c:The condition of your brakes.
note: Stopping distance is made up of your reaction distance and your braking distance. It is affected by things like your reaction time, speed, vehicle weight, brake and tire condition, and the road surface. The time of day by itself does not directly change how far it takes your vehicle to stop, so it is not considered a factor in stopping distance.

question: If an aggressive driver cuts you off in traffic, what is the safest response?
options: a:Flash your headlights to show them they are wrong.,b:Call the police immediately.,c:Stay calm and move out of the aggressive driver's way.
note: When another driver behaves aggressively, your priority is to avoid a confrontation and stay safe. Stay calm, do not make eye contact or gestures, and safely move out of the aggressive driver’s way. Escalating with lights, horn, or arguments can increase the risk of a crash or road rage incident.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two drivers arrive at an open intersection simultaneously, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The driver on the left.,b:The driver going straight.,c:The driver on the right.
note: At an uncontrolled or open intersection where two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. This rule helps prevent confusion and collisions when there are no signs or signals controlling the intersection.

question: Does drinking coffee after drinking alcohol reduce your blood alcohol concentration?
options: a:Yes — it decreases your BAC.,b:No — it has no effect on your BAC.,c:Yes — it cancels the alcohol
note: Coffee will not lower BAC; it may make you more alert but does not change how much alcohol is in your body.

question: When should drivers use hand-to-hand (push/pull) steering?
options: a:When turning the steering wheel during normal driving activities.,b:Only when anti-lock brakes are engaged.,c:Only for low-speed turns.
note: Hand-to-hand (push/pull) steering is the recommended method for most normal driving turns because it helps you keep both hands on the wheel, maintain better control, and avoid crossing your arms in front of the airbag.

question: Why shouldn't you follow other cars too closely?
options: a:You may not see the vehicle's turn signals.,b:You may not see the road between cars.,c:You may not have time to stop if the vehicle ahead slows or stops suddenly.
note: If you follow too closely, you may not have enough time or distance to stop if the vehicle ahead slows or stops suddenly, which greatly increases the risk of a rear-end collision. Always leave enough following distance to react safely.

question: What color are signs that indicate areas of public recreation or cultural interest?
options: a:Orange.,b:Green.,c:Brown.
note: Brown traffic signs are used for guidance to recreational areas, parks, and sites of cultural or historical interest, helping drivers locate these destinations.

question: Which of these does NOT affect your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:The type of alcoholic beverage you drink.,b:How much time passes between drinks.,c:Your body weight.
note: Your blood alcohol concentration (BAC) depends on how much alcohol you consume, how quickly you drink it, your body weight, and how much time your body has to eliminate alcohol. Different types of alcoholic drinks can contain very different amounts of pure alcohol, so what matters is the total amount of alcohol you take in, not the drink’s name or flavor.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before passing another vehicle you should:
options: a:Signal early enough for other drivers to know your plans in advance.,b:Signal after you have changed lanes.,c:Signal just before changing lanes.
note: Before passing, you should signal well in advance so other drivers know you intend to change lanes or move around another vehicle. Early signaling gives them time to adjust speed or position and helps prevent sudden, unexpected movements.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street you should finish the turn into:
options: a:The center of the street.,b:The right lane of the one-way street.,c:The left lane of the one-way street.
note: When turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, you must turn into the lane closest to you on the one-way street. Since you are turning left, that is the left lane of the one-way street. This keeps traffic organized and prevents you from cutting across lanes into the path of other vehicles.

question: What are signs called that require drivers to obey indicated instructions?
options: a:Regulatory signs.,b:Information signs.,c:Warning signs.
note: Regulatory signs tell you what you must do or must not do, such as speed limits, stop, yield, and no-turn signs. These signs are enforceable by law, and failing to obey them can result in citations. Information and warning signs provide guidance or alerts but do not impose legal requirements in the same way.

question: What problems can worn or bald tires cause?
options: a:They improve fuel economy but reduce grip.,b:They only make the ride less comfortable.,c:They can increase stopping distance and make turning more difficult.
note: Worn or bald tires have less tread, which reduces traction with the road. This increases your stopping distance, makes it harder to steer and turn safely, and greatly raises the risk of skidding or hydroplaning on wet roads. Good tread is essential for safe braking and control.

question: Downward-facing triangular traffic signs typically:
options: a:Tell drivers to yield.,b:Indicate construction zones.,c:Indicate a school zone.
note: A downward-pointing triangle is the standard shape for yield signs. It tells you to slow down, be prepared to stop if necessary, and give the right-of-way to traffic in the intersection or on the cross street before you proceed.

question: What color pavement markings separate traffic moving in opposite directions?
options: a:Yellow.,b:Both yellow and white.,c:White.
note: Yellow pavement markings separate traffic moving in opposite directions, such as the center line on a two-way road. White pavement markings separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction and also mark the right edge of the roadway.

question: Traffic lanes moving in opposite directions are divided by lines of what color?
options: a:Red.,b:White.,c:Yellow.
note: Yellow center lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. White lines are used to separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction.

question: In icy or snowy conditions, which of the following choices is most helpful in avoiding a crash?
options: a:Reduce your speed and increase your following distance.,b:Engage the four-wheel drive on your vehicle.,c:Add extra weight to your vehicle to improve traction.
note: In snow or ice, the best way to avoid a crash is to slow down, increase your following distance, and make all movements gently. Four‑wheel drive can help you move or get started, but it does not help you stop or turn on ice and can give a false sense of security. No amount of extra weight or equipment replaces reducing speed and increasing space.

question: How can you verify you are stopped at a safe distance behind another vehicle?
options: a:You can see the ground under the other vehicle’s rear wheels.,b:You can read any bumper stickers.,c:You can read the license plate.
note: When you stop and can see the ground under the rear tires of the vehicle ahead, you have left enough space to steer around it or react if it rolls back. This is a common visual check for a safe stopping distance in traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two vehicles arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, which vehicle must yield?
options: a:The car on the left has the right-of-way.,b:The car on the left shall yield to the car on the right.,c:The largest vehicle has the right-of-way.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection where two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. This rule helps decide who goes first when there are no signs or signals.

question: Why should drivers be extra alert to motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians?
options: a:They always disobey traffic laws.,b:They are often harder to see and may have less noticeable lighting.,c:They follow different rules that exempt them from right-of-way laws.
note: Motorcycles, bicycles, and pedestrians are smaller and can be hidden in blind spots or low light. Because they are less visible and more vulnerable, drivers must scan carefully and give them extra space to prevent collisions.

question: How can you help avoid rear-end collisions?
options: a:Check rearview and blind spots only after braking.,b:Avoid sudden stops and release the gas before braking to slow smoothly.,c:Always brake as hard as possible without warning.
note: To reduce the chance of being rear‑ended, start slowing by easing off the accelerator first, then apply smooth, steady braking. This gives drivers behind you more time to notice that you are slowing and to react safely, instead of being surprised by a sudden hard stop.

question: What does a double solid yellow centerline indicate on a two-lane road?
options: a:Passing is allowed when safe.,b:Traffic moves in the same direction and passing is prohibited.,c:Traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is prohibited.
note: A double solid yellow line in the center of a two‑lane road means traffic flows in opposite directions and passing is not allowed from either direction. You may usually cross these lines only to turn left into or out of a driveway or side road when it is safe and not prohibited by signs.

question: Using which device is associated with a higher risk of driver distraction?
options: a:A cell phone,b:A CD player,c:A radio
note: Using a cell phone while driving, even with hands‑free equipment, greatly increases distraction because it takes your attention and often your eyes and hands away from driving. Radios and CD players can distract you, but normal use is generally less risky than talking, dialing, or texting on a phone.

question: If a vehicle with ABS loses traction on a slippery road, how should the driver brake?
options: a:Pump the brakes.,b:Press and hold the gas pedal to regain traction.,c:Press and hold the brake pedal firmly.
note: In a vehicle with ABS, you should press the brake pedal firmly and hold it down. The ABS system automatically pumps the brakes to prevent wheel lockup and help you maintain steering control. Do not pump the brakes yourself in an ABS‑equipped vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following statements about passing is true?
options: a:Return to your lane only after you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,b:Use your mirrors and look over your left shoulder to check your blind spot when passing to the left.,c:Signal at least 100 feet before changing lanes to pass, unless a different distance is posted.
note: Before passing to the left, signal and check mirrors and the blind spot; do not return to your lane until you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.

question: What should be your first response to reduced visibility?
options: a:Turn on windshield wipers.,b:Turn on your headlights.,c:Reduce your speed.
note: When visibility drops, your stopping distance stays the same but you can see less of the road ahead. Your first reaction should be to slow down so you have more time to react to hazards. After reducing speed, use headlights and wipers as needed so you can see and be seen.

question: How is distracted driving best described?
options: a:Extremely risky behavior that endangers the driver and others.,b:A minor concern with little effect on safety.,c:Very uncommon and not a major problem.
note: Distracted driving means your attention is taken away from driving by things like phones, passengers, eating, or adjusting controls. It greatly increases your chance of a crash and can seriously injure or kill you and others, so it is considered extremely risky behavior.

question: What does a single broken yellow line down the center of a two-lane road mean?
options: a:Lanes move in opposite directions and passing is always prohibited.,b:Lanes move in the same direction and passing is prohibited.,c:Lanes move in opposite directions and passing is allowed when safe.
note: A single broken yellow line in the center means traffic is moving in opposite directions and you may pass another vehicle when it is safe and legal. You must still check for oncoming traffic, ensure you have enough space, and obey any additional signs or markings that restrict passing.

question: If you hear a siren behind you while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up to get out of the way.,b:Stop immediately where you are.,c:Pull over to the right and stop to let the emergency vehicle pass.
note: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights behind you, you must yield the right-of-way. Safely move to the right side of the road and stop until the emergency vehicle has passed, unless a police officer directs you otherwise or you are in an intersection, in which case you clear the intersection first.

question: If you are angry after an incident at work, when you get to your car you should:
options: a:Take a few minutes to cool off before starting your drive home.,b:Drive fast on the interstate to let off steam.,c:Play the radio loudly to drown out thoughts.
note: Strong emotions like anger can distract you and lead to aggressive or risky driving. Before you start driving, take a few minutes to calm down so you can focus on the road, make good decisions, and respond safely to other drivers.

question: A flashing yellow traffic light means drivers should:
options: a:Speed up to clear the intersection quickly.,b:Stop and wait for a green light.,c:Slow down and proceed with caution.
note: A flashing yellow light means there is a potential hazard ahead, but you are not required to stop. You should slow down, be prepared to yield if needed, and proceed through the intersection with extra caution.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to change lanes you should:
options: a:Only check your side view mirror.,b:Quickly turn your head to check without using mirrors.,c:Check side and rearview mirrors and quickly glance over your shoulder for other vehicles.
note: Before changing lanes, first check your rearview and side mirrors to see traffic around you, then quickly glance over your shoulder in the direction you want to move to check your blind spot. Only change lanes when it is clear and safe.

question: When approaching an emergency vehicle stopped with lights flashing, you must:
options: a:Remain in your lane and keep your current speed.,b:Slow down and, if safe, move over to give extra room to the stopped emergency vehicle.,c:Drive to the right side of the road and stop immediately.
note: You must slow down and move over if it is safe to do so to give extra room to emergency, tow, or roadside assistance vehicles; if you cannot move over, slow to a speed below the posted limit.

question: Stop lines painted across traffic lanes indicate:
options: a:Locations next to schools and churches,b:Curves and hills,c:Intersections and pedestrian crosswalks where you must stop.
