note: A stop line is a solid white line painted across the lane at an intersection or before a crosswalk. You must stop with your front bumper behind this line when required by a stop sign or red traffic signal, so pedestrians and cross traffic have space.

question: If your car begins to skid, where should you steer?
options: a:Keep the front wheels straight.,b:In the opposite direction of the skid.,c:In the direction you want the vehicle to go.
note: In a skid, you should look and steer in the direction you want the front of the vehicle to go. As the car begins to straighten out, you may need to steer gently in the opposite direction to avoid overcorrecting and causing another skid.

question: Anything that causes you to do which of these could lead to a crash?
options: a:Only take your hands off the wheel.,b:Only take your eyes off the road.,c:Take your attention away from the task of driving.
note: Anything that takes your mind off driving, your eyes off the road, or your hands off the wheel is a distraction and can lead to a crash. Mental, visual, and manual distractions all increase crash risk.

question: Which statement about railroad crossings is true?
options: a:You do not have to stop when directed to do so by a flagger.,b:It is against the law to go around lowered crossing gates.,c:All railroad crossings are equipped with flashing red signals and gates.
note: You must never drive around or under lowered railroad crossing gates; it is illegal and extremely dangerous. Always obey gates, lights, bells, and any flagger directing traffic at a crossing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When the traffic light turns solid yellow as you approach an intersection, what should you do?
options: a:Consider it the same as a caution sign and continue regardless.,b:Speed up to beat the light.,c:Stop before entering the intersection unless you are too close to stop safely.
note: A solid yellow light means the signal is about to turn red. You must stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely; if you are too close to stop safely, continue through with caution.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: The space needed to cross traffic is determined by which factors?
options: a:Road and weather conditions and oncoming traffic.,b:Whether there is a stop sign present.,c:If your turn signal is in use.
note: To cross traffic safely, you need enough time and space based on how fast other vehicles are coming and how quickly you can accelerate. Poor road or weather conditions mean you need even more space.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning onto a street with multiple lanes in your direction, which lane should you enter?
options: a:The middle lane regardless of where you came from.,b:The lane marked with an arrow only.,c:The lane closest to your previous lane.
note: When turning onto a multi-lane street, you must turn into the lane that is closest to the lane you came from. Complete your turn first, then change lanes later when it is safe and legal.

question: If you encounter an aggressive driver you should:
options: a:Avoid eye contact,b:Retaliate by tailgating.,c:Cut them off to slow them down.
note: If you encounter an aggressive driver, stay calm, avoid eye contact or gestures, and do not respond to their behavior. Create space between your vehicle and theirs, and if necessary, change lanes or exit the roadway safely. Never retaliate, as that can escalate the situation and increase the risk of a crash.

question: Which traffic signal tells you to slow down and proceed with caution through an intersection?
options: a:A solid yellow light,b:A flashing red light,c:A flashing yellow light
note: A flashing yellow light means you must slow down and proceed through the intersection with caution, being prepared to stop if needed. It does not require a full stop, but you must carefully check for other vehicles, pedestrians, or hazards before continuing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a driver's left arm and hand are extended downward, that hand signal means the driver intends to:
options: a:Turn left.,b:Stop.,c:Turn right.
note: Hand signals are used when turn signals are not working or are hard to see. A left arm straight out means a left turn, a left arm bent upward means a right turn, and a left arm extended downward with the palm facing back means the driver intends to stop or slow down.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you enter a freeway safely?
options: a:Signal, use the acceleration lane to match freeway speed, and merge when safe.,b:Signal and then accelerate much faster than traffic.,c:Enter slowly; freeway traffic must yield.
note: To enter a freeway safely, use the entrance ramp and acceleration lane to signal, check mirrors and blind spots, and adjust your speed to match the flow of freeway traffic. Yield to vehicles already on the freeway and merge smoothly when there is a safe gap. Freeway traffic does not have to yield to you, and you should not accelerate far faster than the flow.

question: When approaching a stopped school bus with its stop arm extended, drivers should:
options: a:Proceed if they think children are finished exiting.,b:Honk before passing on the left.,c:Come to a complete stop and wait to proceed.
note: When a school bus displays its stop signal, you must stop and remain stopped until the stop arm is withdrawn.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left you must yield the right-of-way to:
options: a:Oncoming traffic.,b:Other drivers already in the intersection only.,c:Pedestrians already in the intersection only.
note: When turning left, you must yield to oncoming vehicles, pedestrians in the crosswalk, and any traffic already in the intersection. Oncoming traffic going straight or turning right has the right-of-way unless you have a protected green arrow.

question: What do round warning signs usually indicate?
options: a:A no-passing zone.,b:A school zone.,c:An upcoming railroad crossing area.
note: In the U.S., the only standard round warning sign is for a railroad crossing ahead. When you see a round yellow sign with a black X and RR, slow down, look, and listen for trains.

question: What should you adjust first after getting into a car?
options: a:The steering wheel.,b:Your seat.,c:Your rearview mirror.
note: Adjust your seat first so you can reach the pedals, steering wheel, and controls comfortably and see clearly. Once your seating position is correct, then adjust mirrors and steering wheel to match that position.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which traffic signal gives you the right-of-way to turn left?
options: a:A green arrow pointing left.,b:A solid green light.,c:A flashing yellow light.
note: A steady green left arrow gives you a protected left turn. Oncoming traffic has a red light, so you have the right-of-way to turn left, but you must still check the intersection and yield to any pedestrians in your path.

question: What does a flashing yellow arrow for left turns allow you to do?
options: a:Merge into the lane in the arrow direction without yielding.,b:Turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.,c:Come to a complete stop before turning.
note: A flashing yellow left arrow means you may turn left, but only after yielding to oncoming traffic, cyclists, and pedestrians. It is a permissive turn, not a protected one, so you must wait for a safe gap before turning.

question: Which practice helps prevent crashes by communicating with others on the road?
options: a:Drive only on side streets to avoid others.,b:Ignore other drivers and focus only on your lane.,c:Signal your intentions and use horn or emergency signals when appropriate.
note: Communicating clearly with other road users helps prevent crashes. Use your turn signals to show when you plan to turn or change lanes, tap your horn only when needed to alert others, and use emergency flashers when your vehicle is stopped or moving much slower than traffic. This gives others time to react safely.

question: A properly adjusted lap belt should sit:
options: a:Hidden beneath the seat.,b:Snugly across your hip bones and upper thighs, low on the hips.,c:Loosely across your waist.
note: A lap belt should fit low and snug across the hip bones and upper thighs, not the soft abdomen. This positioning helps the strong pelvic bones absorb crash forces and reduces the risk of internal injuries. The belt should never be worn loosely or across the stomach.

question: Before backing out of a driveway where children are playing, what should you do?
options: a:Sound your horn to warn the children.,b:Rev the engine to get their attention.,c:Exit the vehicle and walk to the back to ensure the way is clear.
note: Before backing where children may be present, walk behind your vehicle to check for children, toys, or other obstacles. Do not rely only on mirrors or cameras, because small children can be hidden in blind zones. After checking, back up slowly and be prepared to stop immediately.

question: What is the most common cause of traffic crashes?
options: a:New drivers.,b:Bad weather.,c:Human error.
note: Most crashes are caused by human error, such as inattention, distraction, following too closely, speeding, or failing to yield. While weather and road conditions can contribute, safe and attentive driving usually prevents crashes even in less‑than‑ideal conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What do speed limit signs represent?
options: a:The maximum or minimum legal speed allowed under ideal conditions.,b:Potential driving speeds for the area.,c:A recommended speed only for heavy traffic.
note: Speed limit signs show the maximum (and sometimes minimum) legal speed for that road under ideal conditions. You must slow down below the posted limit when traffic, weather, or road conditions are poor, or when hazards are present.

question: Combining alcohol with drugs usually causes what effect?
options: a:It decreases the effects of both.,b:It helps cure an illness.,c:It increases the effects of both the drugs and the alcohol.
note: Combining alcohol with many drugs is dangerous because the substances can interact and intensify each other’s effects. This can greatly increase drowsiness, slow reaction time, impair judgment, and reduce coordination, making driving extremely unsafe.

question: Why is it important to be alert for motorcycles?
options: a:They are smaller and harder to see and it is difficult to judge their distance and speed.,b:Motorcyclists are less skilled drivers than others.,c:They rarely use headlights.
note: Motorcycles are smaller than other vehicles and can be easily hidden in blind spots or blend into traffic, making them harder to see. It is also more difficult to judge a motorcycle’s speed and distance, so drivers must look carefully and allow extra space.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When the center line shows a solid yellow next to a broken yellow and the broken line is next to you, when may you pass?
options: a:Only on expressways.,b:Only in an emergency.,c:When oncoming traffic is clear.
note: A solid yellow line next to a broken yellow line means that passing is allowed only for traffic on the side with the broken line. If the broken yellow line is next to your lane, you may pass when oncoming traffic is clear and it is safe, legal, and not prohibited by signs or conditions.

question: What will help someone overcome the effects of alcoholic drinks?
options: a:Drinking hot coffee.,b:Allowing time for the body to metabolize the alcohol.,c:Getting fresh air.
note: Only the passage of time will allow a person to eliminate the effects of alcohol; coffee or fresh air do not help.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: As you prepare to make a right turn, your car should be:
options: a:Close to the left side of the street.,b:Near the center of the street.,c:As close to the right side of the road as possible.
note: Before making a right turn, you should safely move your vehicle as close to the right edge or curb as possible. This positioning helps prevent other vehicles from passing you on the right and makes your turn smoother and safer.

question: If another vehicle may hit you, what is an appropriate way to warn them?
options: a:Wave your arms out the window.,b:Use your emergency lights only.,c:Sound your horn to alert the other driver.
note: Sounding your horn is the correct way to warn another driver or pedestrian if they may not see you and a collision could occur. Waving your arms is unreliable and can distract others, and emergency flashers are for breakdowns or hazards, not for immediate collision warning.

question: As a pedestrian, when should you enter a street or crosswalk?
options: a:Enter at any time because it is the driver's responsibility to stop.,b:Always insist on the right-of-way and step into the crosswalk immediately.,c:Only when it is safe to do so and no vehicles are approaching too closely.
note: Pedestrians should only enter a street or crosswalk when it is safe and there is enough distance for approaching vehicles to stop. Even when you have the right-of-way, you must not step into traffic so suddenly that drivers cannot reasonably yield.

question: A stop sign has the shape of a(n):
options: a:Rectangle.,b:Circle.,c:Octagon.
note: Stop signs are uniquely octagonal so drivers can recognize them easily, even from the back or in poor visibility. When you see this eight-sided shape, you must come to a complete stop at the appropriate stopping point.

question: When is it acceptable to park in the access aisle next to a reserved handicap parking space?
options: a:When all other parking spaces are full.,b:When you have a handicap plate or placard.,c:Never.
note: The striped access aisle next to a handicap space is reserved for wheelchair lifts and extra space for people with disabilities to enter and exit vehicles. It is illegal to park there at any time, even if you have a disability placard or the lot is crowded.

question: What does a regulatory sign with a red circle and slash indicate?
options: a:The action shown is forbidden.,b:That some drivers must yield to others.,c:Drivers must come to a complete stop.
note: A regulatory sign with a red circle and a diagonal slash over a symbol means that the pictured action is prohibited. For example, a right-turn arrow with a red slash means no right turn is allowed at that location.

question: If your tire suddenly blows out while driving, you should:
options: a:Slam on your brakes immediately.,b:Keep driving at the same speed.,c:Hold the steering wheel firmly and gradually slow to a stop.
note: If a tire blows out, keep a firm grip on the steering wheel, stay off the brakes at first, and gently ease your foot off the accelerator. Let the vehicle slow down gradually while you maintain control and steer straight. Once you are moving slowly and the vehicle is stable, brake lightly and move to a safe place off the road.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two vehicles arrive at a four-way stop at the same time, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:Both must yield and make hand signals.,b:The vehicle on the left.,c:The vehicle on the right.
note: At a four‑way stop, when two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. The vehicle on the right has the right‑of‑way and may proceed first when it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Approaching a steady green light, what should a driver do?
options: a:Stop if a police officer is nearby.,b:Treat it like a four-way stop.,c:Proceed if the intersection is clear and yield to pedestrians or vehicles still in the intersection.
note: A steady green light means you may go straight or turn, if it is safe, but you must still yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk and to any vehicles already in the intersection. Approach at a speed that allows you to react if the light changes or if someone is still in the intersection.

question: A person using a white cane or a guide dog is most likely to be:
options: a:A blind person.,b:A deaf person.,c:A person involved with a traffic study.
note: A person using a white cane or a guide dog is almost always a blind or visually impaired pedestrian. Drivers must always yield the right‑of‑way, stop if necessary, and use extra caution around these pedestrians, never honking or revving the engine in a way that could startle them.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a fire engine is following you but not using emergency signals, how should you respond?
options: a:Speed up to get out of its path.,b:Stop immediately to let it pass.,c:Continue driving normally; you do not need to clear the way.
note: You are required to yield and clear the way for emergency vehicles only when they are using their lights and/or siren. If a fire engine is behind you without emergency signals, simply continue driving normally, obeying all traffic laws and not making sudden or unpredictable maneuvers.

question: What affects your ability to stop your vehicle?
options: a:The road and weather conditions (road condition).,b:Signal lights.,c:The time of day.
note: Your stopping ability is strongly affected by road and weather conditions because they change how much traction your tires have. On wet, icy, or gravel roads, it takes much longer to stop than on dry pavement. Signal lights or time of day do not directly change how quickly your vehicle can stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a steady green light at an intersection authorize you to do?
options: a:Proceed through the intersection if the road is clear.,b:Must stop and check for oncoming traffic.,c:Always slow and prepare to stop.
note: A steady green light means you are permitted to go straight or turn, but only if the intersection is clear. You must still yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk and to any vehicles already in the intersection or lawfully within the intersection when the light turned green.

question: When does your vehicle's stopping distance increase?
options: a:On wet or icy roads.,b:On dry paved highways.,c:Only when driving at night.
note: Stopping distance increases when traction is reduced, such as on wet, icy, or snowy roads, and when you are driving faster. On slippery roads your tires cannot grip the surface as well, so you need more distance to come to a complete stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before changing lanes you should check your blind spots by:
options: a:Turning your head to look over your shoulder.,b:Using only the outside rearview mirror.,c:Using only the inside rearview mirror.
note: Every vehicle has blind spots that mirrors cannot show. Before changing lanes, you must check your mirrors and then quickly turn your head to look over your shoulder in the direction of the lane change to be sure no vehicle is in your blind spot.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do if you arrive at an intersection wanting to turn but are not in the correct lane?
options: a:Quickly cut across traffic to make the turn.,b:Turn on your blinker and turn from your current lane.,c:Drive to the next intersection and make the turn from the proper lane.
note: If you are not in the correct lane to turn, continue straight and make your turn at the next intersection from the proper lane. Sudden lane changes or turning from the wrong lane can surprise other drivers and cause collisions.

question: If an approaching train is close enough to be a danger, you must:
options: a:Cross the tracks at your own risk.,b:Slow down and proceed with caution.,c:Not cross the tracks until the train has completely passed.
note: When a train is approaching and close enough to be a danger, you must stop and wait. Never try to beat the train or cross while it is approaching. Do not proceed until the train has completely passed, the tracks are clear in both directions, and all warning devices (lights, gates, bells) have stopped operating.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: The holder of a New Hampshire Youth Operator license under the age of 18 is not allowed to operate a motor vehicle between which hours?
options: a:12:00 a.m. (midnight) and 5:00 a.m.,b:1:00 a.m. and 4:00 a.m.,c:11:00 p.m. and 6:00 a.m.
note: Under New Hampshire law, a Youth Operator license holder under the age of 18 cannot operate a motor vehicle between the hours of 1:00 a.m. and 4:00 a.m.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: In New Hampshire, what is the minimum age at which you may practice driving a non-commercial vehicle when accompanied by a licensed parent, guardian, or designated adult?
options: a:15 years of age.,b:16 years of age.,c:15 1/2 years of age.
note: New Hampshire does not issue a learner's permit. A resident may practice driving once they reach 15 1/2 years of age, provided they carry proof of age and are supervised in the front seat by a licensed parent, guardian, or adult age 25 or older.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: During the first 6 months after receiving a Youth Operator license, the driver under 18 cannot operate a vehicle with more than how many passengers under age 25 who are not family members?
options: a:No passengers under age 25.,b:Only one passenger under age 25.,c:Up to three passengers under age 25.
note: During the first 6 months after receiving a Youth Operator license, a driver under 18 cannot drive with more than one passenger under age 25 who is not an immediate family member, unless accompanied by a licensed adult age 25 or older.

question: Under New Hampshire law, a moped is defined as a motor-driven cycle that cannot exceed what speed on level ground?
options: a:25 miles per hour.,b:30 miles per hour.,c:35 miles per hour.
note: In New Hampshire, a moped is defined as having an engine of 50 cc or less, 2 horsepower or less, and it must not require shifting gears. It cannot exceed a speed of 30 mph on level ground.

question: New Hampshire law requires headlights to be turned on from 1/2 hour after sunset to 1/2 hour before sunrise, and whenever visibility is less than:
options: a:500 feet.,b:1,000 feet.,c:150 feet.
note: You must turn on your headlights from 1/2 hour after sunset to 1/2 hour before sunrise, or anytime weather or road conditions reduce visibility so you cannot see clearly for 1,000 feet.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Unless otherwise posted, what is the minimum speed you may drive on a New Hampshire interstate highway under normal weather and road conditions?
options: a:45 miles per hour.,b:50 miles per hour.,c:40 miles per hour.
note: In New Hampshire, the minimum speed you may drive on an interstate highway is 45 mph under normal conditions, unless road and weather conditions are so bad that this speed is unsafe.
